79:     @Override
80:     public void setProperty(int nodeId, int property, int valueType, Object value) {
81:         int b = (valueType << 16) | (property & 0xFFFF);
82:         if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
83:             int ref = core.arenaAlloc(handle, ((String) value).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
84:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, ref);
85:         } else if (valueType == ValueTypes.DESIGN_TOKEN) {
86:             int ref = core.arenaAlloc(handle, ((Color) value).token().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
87:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, ref);
88:         } else {
89:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b,
90:                     ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value));
91:         }
92:     }
93: 
94:     @Override
95:     public void setDate(int nodeId, int days, int millisOfDay) {
96:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_DATE, 0, nodeId, days, millisOfDay);
97:     }
98: 
99:     @Override
100:     public void setDesignToken(String path, int valueType, Object value) {
101:         int pathRef = core.arenaAlloc(handle, path.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
102:         int c;
103:         if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
104:             c = core.arenaAlloc(handle, ((String) value).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
105:         } else {
106:             c = ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value);
107:         }
108:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_DESIGN_TOKEN, 0, pathRef, valueType, c);
109:     }

112:         core.push(handle, new Opcode(category, command, flags, a, b, c).toBytes());
113:     }

116:     public void close() {
117:         core.destroy(handle);
118:     }

188:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
189:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
190:                         if !p.children.contains(&child) {
191:                             p.children.push(child);
192:                         }
193:                     }
194:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
195:                         c.parent = Some(parent);
196:                     }
197:                 }
198:                 (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
199:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
200:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
201:                         p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
202:                     }
203:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
204:                         c.parent = None;
205:                     }
206:                 }
207:                 (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => {
208:                     let (parent, child, new_index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c() as usize);
209:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
210:                         if let Some(pos) = p.children.iter().position(|c| *c == child) {
211:                             p.children.remove(pos);
212:                         }
213:                         let idx = if new_index == usize::MAX {
214:                             p.children.len()
215:                         } else {
216:                             new_index.min(p.children.len())
217:                         };
218:                         p.children.insert(idx, child);
219:                     }
220:                 }
221:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_PROPERTY) => {
222:                     let prop_id = op.b() as u16;
223:                     let vt = (op.b() >> 16) as u8;
224:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
225:                         if vt == value_type::STRING {
226:                             // Resolve the arena offset into the actual text.
227:                             if let Ok(text) = frame.arena_str(op.c()) {
228:                                 n.strings.insert(prop_id, text.to_string());
229:                             }
230:                         } else if vt == value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN {
231:                             // A token reference: keep the path for resolution
232:                             // against the theme (spec/TOKENS.md). C is the arena
233:                             // offset of the token path.
234:                             if let Ok(path) = frame.arena_str(op.c()) {
235:                                 n.token_refs.insert(prop_id, path.to_string());
236:                             }
237:                         } else {
238:                             n.properties.insert(prop_id, op.c());
239:                         }
240:                     }
241:                 }
242:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_TEXT) => {
243:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
244:                         n.text = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok().map(|s| s.to_string());
245:                     }
246:                 }
247:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => {
248:                     // Global override: A = arenaRef (token path), B = valueType,
249:                     // C = value (for STRING, an arenaRef to the value string).
250:                     if let Ok(path) = frame.arena_str(op.a()) {
251:                         let vt = (op.b() & 0xFF) as u8;
252:                         let value = if vt == value_type::STRING {
253:                             frame
254:                                 .arena_str(op.c())
255:                                 .map(|s| TokenValue::Str(s.to_string()))
256:                                 .unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(0))
257:                         } else {
258:                             TokenValue::from_wire(vt, op.c()).unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(op.c()))
259:                         };
260:                         if let Some(bare) = path.strip_prefix("dark.") {
261:                             self.dark_overrides.insert(bare.to_string(), value);
262:                         } else {
263:                             self.overrides.insert(path.to_string(), value);
264:                         }
265:                     }
266:                 }
267:                 _ => {}
268:             }
269:         }
270:         self.resolve_tokens();
271:     }

content.text:
I've completed a deep investigation. Here's what I found and the plan I propose.

## Diagnosis

**Two independent problems** make the Qt renderer show practically nothing, and the Java demo (`QtHost` + `SplitNavDemo`) is the sharpest case:

**1. JVM crash — hard blocker (Java path).** `lib/java/pathland-qt-demo/hs_err_pid20903.log` (committed with Phase D, never fixed) is a SIGSEGV in `pathland_qt::run::pump_once` at `qt_tick` (the 0 ms idle timer) while dereferencing the `Runner`'s `dyn Pump` vtable. The app runs ~7s then dies. `pump_once`/`qt_tick` are unchanged since that build, so it's almost certainly still current.

**2. Collapsed layout — "renders practically nothing".** Several concrete bugs in `qt_layer.cpp`:
- **FILL is applied to the wrong parent.** The Rust `diff()` emits props *before* child inserts, and `CREATE_NODE` parents every widget to the window contentItem; so `applySize()` eagerly anchors FILL (`-1`) widgets to the *window*, then they get reparented into a Row/Column with stale anchors (Qt warnings + wrong sizes). Phase D's "defer FILL" only defers when the parent is a positioner *at apply time* — which never happens.
- **Stacks can't stretch children.** Plain `Row`/`Column` (no `QtQuick.Layouts`) reject `anchors.fill` on children and never expand a child. SplitNavDemo's content area is `ScrollView(Navigation.of(router))` with no size hint inside the root `HStack` → it collapses to ~0. `status.md` already flags this gap. The sidebar (fixed 200 px) is all that can appear → "practically nothing".
- **Root never fills the window** (GTK sets hexpand/vexpand; Qt leaves the root Row/Column at (0,0) implicit size).
- **Font props silently fail**: `setProperty("font.pixelSize"|"font.weight"|"font.family")` — `QObject::setProperty` doesn't resolve dotted paths.
- **ScrollView content** is attached to the ScrollView itself, not its `contentItem`.

Qt is 6.11.2 with `QtQuick.Layouts` available.

## Proposed plan

1. **Reproduce** — build `libpathland_core`/`libpathland_qt`, run `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` capturing stderr; confirm crash + collapsed render. (Rust demo as comparison.)
2. **Fix the crash** — reproduce, then harden `pump_once`/`Runner` lifetime + the C++ nav adapter's `deleteLater`/`pending_fill` stale-pointer paths.
3. **Fix layout** — always defer FILL to insert time (`flushFill`), anchor roots to fill the contentItem, map stacks to `RowLayout`/`ColumnLayout` (`FILL → Layout.fillWidth/fillHeight`), attach ScrollView content to `contentItem`, apply fonts via the `QFont` property. Update the passing offscreen FFI tests.
4. **Verify** — Java Qt demo renders the full SplitNavDemo (sidebar + Home/Kitchen/Settings + navigation) with no crash; `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` and `mvn install` stay green; update `pathland-render-qt/status.md`.

One question so I prioritize correctly:

content.text:
Confirmed — "only a sliver of content" means the layout collapse is the main issue (the crash log is secondary but should still be hardened since it can trigger on interaction/re-emit). Here's the final plan.

## Plan: fix Qt renderer — "only a sliver of content"

### 1. Fix FILL sizing (the core sliver cause)
- **`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`:** make `applySize()` for `WIDTH/HEIGHT == -1` (FILL) **always** record `pending_fill` and apply it in `flushFill()` at insert time (on the real parent), never eagerly against the window contentItem. This removes stale-anchor reparenting and the "FILL-in-Row" warnings.
- **Root fill:** anchor root nodes (children of `CONTENT_ITEM`/contentItem) to fill the window, mirroring GTK's hexpand/vexpand, so the SplitNavDemo HStack fills 1100×720.

### 2. Make stacks stretch children (QtQuick.Layouts)
- Map `VSTACK/HSTACK` (incl. lazy variants) to **`ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`import QtQuick.Layouts`), translating:
  - `WIDTH FILL` → `Layout.fillWidth: true`, `HEIGHT FILL` → `Layout.fillHeight: true`
  - positive `WIDTH/HEIGHT` → `Layout.preferredWidth/Height`
  - `SPACING`/`PADDING`/`ALIGNMENT` stay on the layout
- This is what makes the `ScrollView` content area stretch to the remaining row width instead of collapsing to ~0 — the actual "sliver" fix.
- Update the passing offscreen FFI tests (`renderer_drives_live_qml_scene`, `control_widgets_construct_and_apply_props`, etc.) that assert child counts/props — the scene structure is unchanged, but `qmlFor` strings and any `setProperty` targeting change.

### 3. Fix the other property/geometry bugs in `qt_layer.cpp`
- **ScrollView:** attach children to the ScrollView's `contentItem`, not the ScrollView item, so content sizes/scrolls it.
- **Fonts:** apply `FONT_SIZE/FONT_WEIGHT/FONT_FAMILY` via the `font` `QFont` property (get → modify → set), not dotted-path `setProperty`.
- **Nav adapter:** erase `pending_fill` on `promoteNavSlot`/nav page swaps and guard the reconcile path (defensive against the UAF behind the `pump_once` crash log).

### 4. Harden the crash (secondary)
- Investigate/fix the SIGSEGV in `pump_once` (`Runner` vtable deref on the 0 ms timer): verify the `Runner`/`user` lifetime across C++ teardown and the nav adapter's `deleteLater` paths; make the idle timer tolerant so a stale tick can't deref freed memory.

### 5. Verify
- `cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-qt`, then run **`scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`** — expect the full SplitNavDemo (sidebar + Home/Kitchen/Settings content area, navigation) with no crash and no Qt anchor warnings.
- `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` and `cd lib/java && mvn install` stay green.
- Update `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/status.md` (FILL/Layouts/ScrollView/font fixes) per AGENTS.md.

Shall I proceed with this plan?
go

content.text: Wait. qt_layer.cpp return handwritten code. Why? Is thre no api?

Good question. The C++ layer *does* use Qt APIs — it's just that Qt Quick's object model is **QML-first**, so dynamically building UI from C++ goes through `QQmlComponent` (compile a QML snippet per node) plus `QObject::setProperty` for values. There is no C++ factory like `new QQuickColumn()` / `new Button(text)` that's part of the supported API — the QML types (`Column`, `Row`, `Text`, `Button`, …) are only instantiable from QML, so the renderer emits a small QML string per Pathland component and hands it to `QQmlComponent::setData()` (`qt_layer.cpp:179` `createComponent`).

What's genuinely "hand-written" and unavoidable is the **mapping table**: translating Pathland's numeric property IDs (`0x0001` spacing, `0x100B` width, …) and semantics (`-1` = FILL → `anchors.fill`/`Layout.fillWidth`, padding, alignment) onto Qt's per-type properties. That's per-protocol logic — no generic API exists to do that, in any renderer (the GTK and HTML renderers have the same hand-written mapping in Rust).

The part I'm adding now (RowLayout/ColumnLayout + `Layout.fillWidth`) uses Qt's real Layouts API via the private header `qquicklayout_p.h` — the documented C++ accessor for the `Layout` attached properties.

  handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
  activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`

  `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger

  `ALIGNMENT` is applied to each child via its `Layout` attached properties
  (`Fill` stretches the cross axis; Start/Center/End set `Layout.alignment`).

1: # pathland-demo-views — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** September 3, 2026
4: 
5: The framework-agnostic shared demo views (`com.pathland.demo`), consumed by the
6: Quarkus and Spring Boot demos. Uses `State` fields wired by the
7: `pathland-view-processor` annotation processor.
8: 
9: ## Implemented
10: 
11: - **`KitchenSinkView`** (the demo root): a scrollable column of every protocol
12:   section, mounted by both demos' `SessionApp`.
13: - **Sections** (each a custom `View`):
14:   - `SectionCard` — reusable titled/bordered/rounded section wrapper.
15:   - `CounterSection` — `State<Integer>` + `Button` + `Stepper`.
16:   - `TextFieldSection` — `TextField` + `TextEditor` on one `State<String>`.
17:   - `ToggleSection` — `Toggle` in all three `ToggleStyle`s.
18:   - `ValueControlsSection` — `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`ProgressView` on one
19:     `State<Float>`.
20:   - `PickerSection` — `Picker` (Segmented + Menu) + `Menu`.
21:   - `ColorSection` — `ColorPicker` + `Color` as a View + reactive `Rectangle`.
22:   - `DateSection` — `DatePicker` bound to days-since-epoch.
23:   - `LayoutSection` — `Grid`/`LazyVStack`/`HStack`+`Spacer`/`ZStack`/`Divider`.
24:   - `TextStylesSection` — text-formatting modifiers.
25:   - `AppearanceSection` — border/shadow/opacity/transform/hidden/z-index.
26:   - `ThemeSection` — **design-token demo**: `Color.token("color.primary")`,
27:     `Color.token("control.accent")`, `Color.token("color.surface")` /
28:     `Color.token("dark.color.surface")` and a `control.background`-referenced
29:     fill, resolving against the active scheme.
30: - **`DemoTheme`** — the demo's global `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` theme (base + `dark.*`:
31:   `color.primary`, `color.surface`, `color.accent`, `space.base`,
32:   `font.body.family`, `control.*`). Both demos' `SessionApp` pass it to the
33:   `Emitter`, which rides the overrides into the mount (SSR) + resync frames so
34:   the HTML/JS client re-themes under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`.
35: - **Legacy views kept**: `CounterView`, `CounterControls`, `NameField` (still
36:   covered by `CounterViewTest`).
37: - **`SplitNavDemo`** — the demo **root** (spec PRIMITIVES.md:
38:   `NavigationSplitView` → `HStack` sidebar + detail): a fixed menu column on
39:   the left (3 items: Home / Kitchen sink / Settings) and a
40:   `NavigationContainer` content area on the right that swaps on selection
41:   (`router.navigate` — direct selection, no back-stack growth). Mounted directly
42:   by both demos' `SessionApp` with the active platform path provided as an
43:   environment value — **`new SplitNavDemo().environment(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH,
44:   activePath)`**; `SplitNavDemo.body()` reads it and builds a **bound** router
45:   (`Navigation.navigator()...build(activePath)`) — external path changes are
46:   guard-processed and navigation is mirrored back into the signal. The view is
47:   router-free (no app factory / `NavigationApp`).
48:   `SessionApp` seeds `activePath` from the applied
49:   `META::ENVIRONMENT` `ROUTE` field (a request URL on SSR, the DOM client's
50:   first message on the WebSocket), so deep links render correctly on the first
51:   frame; env re-routing sets `activePath`, `NAVIGATE`-with-URL sets `activePath`,
52:   and `NAVIGATE`-back forwards into `RenderResult.navigateHandler`. The view also
53:   demonstrates **`onPathChange`** (logging the active path). The
54:   active menu row is highlighted **reactively** via `Navigation.isActive(router,
55:   path)` → a computed signal that drives `Background.of(Signal<Color>)` /
56:   `ForegroundStyle.of(Signal<Color>)`, so a selection re-emits only that row's
57:   color properties. Content areas are router-free, self-contained views
58:   instantiated inline in the route table:
59:   - `HomeView` — titled welcome pane with a declarative `.navigate("/kitchen")`
60:     button (spec DSL.md §4.5 — a component inside the container changing the
61:     route without a router) (`/` and `/home`).
62:   - `KitchenSinkView` — the full showcase (`/kitchen`).
63:   - `SettingsView` — a switch + volume slider on local signals (`/settings`).
64:   - A `fallback` ("Not Found") for any other path.
65: 
66: - **Semantic accessibility roles** (`AccessibilityRole.of(Roles.*)`,
67:   `com.pathland.view.Roles`): the demo root views carry the `MAIN` landmark
68:   (`HomeView`/`SettingsView`/`KitchenSinkView`/`CounterView`), the sidebar is
69:   `NAVIGATION`, and `SectionCard` titles are `HEADER` headings — the web
70:   renderer reflects these as native semantic elements (`<nav>`, `<main>`,
71:   `<h2>`). Sidebar menu rows are **real `Button`s styled with
72:   `PlainButtonStyle`** (`Button.of(Label, action)`) — control semantics are
73:   intrinsic to the component, not a `ROLE`; a custom-looking button is a
74:   `Button` + `ButtonStyle`.
75: - **Real asset refs**: the demo icons are now actual SVGs served from the
76:   reserved asset mount (`/_pathland/assets/icons/*.svg`) and referenced
77:   **absolute** (fixing the relative-path bug on deep routes).
78: - **`MediaSection`** (kitchensink): a `Video` + `Audio` node with remote sample
79:   URLs — playback interaction is renderer-native (`controls`); the app supplies
80:   only the source + size.
81: 
82: ## Not implemented / gaps
83: 
84: - The browser experience depends on the `@pathland/dom-renderer` client
85:   (`lib/typescript`, built to `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` and copied into
86:   each demo's `src/main/resources`).
87: 
88: ## Verified by
89: 
90: `mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views` (JDK 17+) — `CounterViewTest`,
91: `KitchenSinkViewTest` (mount + persistence + input routing), and
92: `SplitNavDemoTest` (sidebar + content first frame, `/kitchen` content swap,
93: menu-click content swap deltas, reactive active-row highlight). Both SSR demos
94: are verified by running them and curling the deep links (`/`, `/home`,
95: `/kitchen`, `/settings` render the splitview seeded at that path with the right
96: content + `data-pathland-route`; unknown paths show the sidebar + "Not Found";
97: the JS bundle serves correctly).

content.text:
Here's what's needed, based on the current state of the code.

## The gap

Today `Audio` is **renderer-native only**: it maps to `<audio controls>` (`pathland-render-html` / the TS client both set `controls=true`), and the protocol has **no media control channel** (app → renderer: play/pause/seek/volume) and **no media event channel** (renderer → app: time, ended, volume). So the custom Apple-Music `PlayerBar` is pure app state — nothing drives a real audio element.

The event plumbing that *would* carry audio events already exists: the DOM client encodes raw `EVENT` opcodes (`events.ts`) and sends them over the WebSocket (`transport.ts`), and the server routes them into bound `State` via `InputDispatcher`/`RenderResult` (`valueInputs`, `textInputs`, …). Media just needs the same treatment.

## Two ways to get real music

**Option A — Real sound today, native controls (~½ day, zero protocol change).**
Add an `Audio.of(computed(currentTrack))` node (renderer-native `<audio controls>`, small/hidden) plus real audio files. Selecting a track swaps the source via the existing `AUDIO_SOURCE` binding. Actual music plays — but the custom transport buttons stay decoupled from it.

**Option B — App-driven media channel (the proper fix, ~3–5 days, cross-cutting).** This makes the custom PlayerBar *actually drive* the audio, Apple-Music style:
1. **Spec-first** (`spec/`): Audio/Video become app-driven. New control properties (`PLAYBACK_STATE`, `MEDIA_POSITION`/seek, `MEDIA_VOLUME`) + new host→guest events in `EVENTS.md` (`MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED`, `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED`, `MEDIA_ENDED`, `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED`) + CONFORMANCE vectors.
2. **Rust HTML renderer**: emit `<audio>` **without** `controls` (hidden), so only the app UI controls it.
3. **TS DOM client**: apply `PLAYBACK_STATE`→`play()/pause()`, `MEDIA_POSITION`→`currentTime`, `MEDIA_VOLUME`→`volume`; listen for `play/pause/timeupdate/ended/volumechange` and emit the new `EVENT` opcodes over the existing WS path.
4. **Java DSL**: a bound audio surface (`Audio.of(src).playback(playing).position(position).volume(volume)`) emitting the control properties + a `mediaInputs` registry; `InputDispatcher` routes `MEDIA_*` into `State` (and `MEDIA_ENDED` → next track). Echo-suppressed so programmatic sets don't loop.
5. **Server core**: dispatch the new media events (small, mirrors value/text).
6. **Demo**: real royalty-free track files under `/_pathland/assets/audio/` in both demo modules; PlayerBar drives them.
7. **Tests**: conformance vectors, TS audio apply/event test, Java bound-audio + routing test.

Desktop renderers (GTK/Qt) would need the same media channel later — out of scope here since this is the HTML path.

## One thing I need from you

**Audio source**: do you have real music files to ship, or should I source short royalty-free clips (bundled as demo assets), or point at remote sample URLs?

Which direction do you want — A (quick native-controls sound), B (full app-driven media channel), or A now + B later?

B.: Regarding emitting without controls, it should emit with native controls if no children are specified. Similar to button and its buttonStyle, both audio and video should take a Style (AudioStyle and VideoStyle) to be able to define custom controls.
Let me study the Button/ButtonStyle machinery to mirror it for Audio/Video.

95: ### Pointer
96: 
97: Pointer events carry a viewport-relative point in **logical points** (`B`=x,
98: `C`=y, f32).
99: 
100: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
101: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
102: | `POINTER_DOWN` | 0x01 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | press (basis of `onTapGesture`, `Button` action) |
103: | `POINTER_MOVE` | 0x02 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` (0x0001) / `HOVER_LEAVE` (0x0002) | hover/enter/leave, drag basis |
104: | `POINTER_UP` | 0x03 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | release (basis of `onTapGesture`) |
105: 
106: - **Flags**:
107:   - `POINTER_SECONDARY`: the secondary button (right mouse, long-press) rather
108:     than the primary.
109:   - `HOVER_ENTER` (bit 0 of `POINTER_MOVE`): the pointer just entered the
110:     node's bounds (is now hovering). `HOVER_LEAVE` (bit 1): the pointer just
111:     left. A plain move has neither bit set.
112: - **Listener bits**: `POINTER_DOWN` (bit 0), `POINTER_MOVE` (bit 1),
113:   `POINTER_UP` (bit 2).
114: - **Renderer**: attaches native press/hover recognition to the matching native
115:   element when the listener bit is set. Multiple pointer events may be reported
116:   for one physical gesture (down → several moves → up), all for the same
117:   `targetId` while the pointer stays over the node.
118: 
119: ### Keyboard
120: 
121: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
122: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
123: | `KEY_DOWN` | 0x04 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` (0x0002) | `onKeyPress(.down)` |
124: | `KEY_UP` | 0x05 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | `onKeyPress(.up)` |
125: 
126: - **`keyCode`**: a **canonical, platform-independent logical key code** (a
127:   renderer maps native scancodes/key-codes onto this canonical set). The
128:   canonical set (letters/digits/arrows/Enter/Tab/…) is renderer-shared and
129:   documented in the conformance vectors.
130: - **`modifiers`**: u8 bitmask — `Shift`=0x01, `Control`=0x02, `Alt`=0x04,
131:   `Meta/Super`=0x08.
132: - **`KEY_REPEAT`**: bit 1 of flags; set when the key is an OS auto-repeat.
133: - **Listener bits**: `KEY_DOWN` (bit 3), `KEY_UP` (bit 4).
134: - **Focus**: keyboard events are reported to the focused node (the node that
135:   most recently gained focus), or to the node that declared the listener and
136:   has keyboard focus. See `FOCUS_CHANGED` below.
137: 
138: ### Value
139: 
140: Value events carry a control's semantic value, resolved by the renderer from
141: its own native control geometry.
142: 
143: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
144: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
145: | `VALUE_CHANGED` | 0x06 | targetId | value (f32) | 0 | — | `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`Toggle`/`Picker`/`Menu` binding changes |
146: 
147: - **Semantics per control** (see [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) controls):
148:   - `SLIDER`/`STEPPER`/`GAUGE` — the numeric value in the control's range.
149:   - `TOGGLE` — 0/1 (checked state; the same value the app writes to
150:     `SELECTED`).
151:   - `PICKER`/`MENU` — the selected option/action-item index.
152:   - `COLOR_PICKER` — the packed `0xAARRGGBB` color reinterpreted as an f32 bit
153:     pattern.
154:   - `DATE_PICKER` uses the dedicated `DATE_CHANGED` event below (its value is
155:     two fields and does not fit `VALUE_CHANGED`).
156: - The app writes the received value into its bound `State`; the engine's
157:   signal flush re-emits the `SET_PROPERTY` delta back to the renderer (the
158:   renderer reflects its own native control).
159: - **No listener bit**: value-bearing controls are reported by the renderer by
160:   virtue of their component type, but still gated by the transport-aware event
161:   guards (a control without `BINDING_ID` reports nothing). The renderer owns

163: 
164: ### Date
165: 
166: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
167: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
168: | `DATE_CHANGED` | 0x0D | targetId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | `DatePicker` value binding |
169: 
170: - The date is encoded as two 32-bit fields — `B` = **days since epoch**
171:   (signed I32; pre-1970 is negative) and `C` = **millis of day** (U32,
172:   0..86,400,000) — matching the `STYLE::SET_DATE` command (OPCODE.md). No
173:   string/arena indirection: the event is fully inline. It works over the
174:   shared-memory ring today and will use the same inline encoding for host →
175:   guest network batches once that direction lands (see OPCODE.md Transport).
176: - **No listener bit**: like `VALUE_CHANGED`, reported by virtue of the
177:   component type.
178: 
179: ### Text
180: 
181: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
182: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
183: | `TEXT_CHANGED` | 0x07 | targetId | string offset | 0 | — | `TextField` value binding |
184: | `FOCUS_CHANGED` | 0x08 | targetId | focused (0/1) | 0 | — | `@FocusState` |
185: | `EDITING_CHANGED` | 0x09 | targetId | editing (0/1) | 0 | — | `TextField`/`Slider` `onEditingChanged` |

## Design-Token Resolution Conformance

The token system (catalog, override/default resolution, `dark.` color-scheme
layer) is defined in [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md). Resolution is a renderer behavior
and is not byte-encodable; a conforming renderer MUST produce these outcomes.

Given the overrides:

| Token override (via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) | Value |
|------------------------------------------|-------|
| `color.primary` | `0xFF2563EB` |
| `dark.color.primary` | `0xFF60A5FA` |
| `space.base` | `4.0` (F32) |

| Query | Active scheme | Resolves to | Rationale |
|-------|---------------|-------------|-----------|
| `color.primary` | dark | `0xFF60A5FA` | `dark.color.primary` override wins (dark layer) |
| `color.primary` | light | `0xFF2563EB` | dark layer skipped; base override wins |
| `color.primary` | dark, no `dark.*` override | base override `0xFF2563EB` | base override falls through when the dark layer is empty |
| `font.body.size` | either | renderer default | no override; defaults are renderer-owned |
| `font.body.size` | either, override only `font.body` | the `font.body` override | parent-path fallback |
| `space.2` | either | `8.0` | generative family: `space.base` (4.0) × 2 |
| `space.0.5` | either | `2.0` | generative family: fractional leaf |
| `space.2` | either, `space.base` not overridden | renderer default × 2 | generative base falls back to renderer defaults |

A property carrying the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (vector 18) resolves through
the same algorithm and MUST re-resolve when the active scheme changes.

### Navigation

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
| --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `NAVIGATE` | 0x0E | 0 | URL string offset | 0 | `NAVIGATE_URL` (0x0001) | browser back/forward (`popstate`), a deep link, or a native back affordance |

### Media

Media events report a `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` node's playback state back to the app
(target = the media node id). They are reported by the renderer by virtue of the
media node's component type — no listener bit, mirroring `VALUE_CHANGED` — and
only when the app has bound the corresponding control property (so a
renderer-native `<audio controls>` reports nothing).

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
| --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` | 0x0F | targetId | playing (0/1) | 0 | — | `AVPlayer` play/pause |
| `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` | 0x10 | targetId | seconds (f32) | 0 | — | periodic time observer |
| `MEDIA_ENDED` | 0x11 | targetId | 0 | 0 | — | `AVPlayerItemDidPlayToEndTime` |
| `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` | 0x12 | targetId | volume (f32, 0..1) | 0 | — | `AVPlayer.volume` |

- **`MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED`**: the media's current playback position in seconds.
  Reported periodically while playing; a seek initiated by the app
  (`MEDIA_POSITION` change) is not echoed back.
- **Guards**: media events flow only when the app bound the matching control
  property (`PLAYBACK_STATE`/`MEDIA_POSITION`/`MEDIA_VOLUME`) on the node; a
  plain `<audio controls>` reports nothing.

input.newString:
### Audio — `AUDIO` 0x09

An audio playback node. Playback is **renderer-native by default** (the web
renderer emits `controls`); the app supplies the source reference. A **custom
`AudioStyle`** supplies app-driven control children (transport buttons, seek,
volume) — the node then carries the media control properties below and the
renderer renders a hidden media element alongside the custom controls.

- **Protocol**: a leaf node by default (no children); source via `AUDIO_SOURCE`
  (0x1033, STRING: a resource name, file path, or absolute URL — an asset
  reference, never embedded in the opcode stream). With a custom style the
  node's children are the custom control UI.
- **Properties**: `AUDIO_SOURCE`, the media control properties —
  `PLAYBACK_STATE` (0x1035, U32 0/1), `MEDIA_POSITION` (0x1036, F32 seconds;
  a change seeks), `MEDIA_VOLUME` (0x1037, F32 0..1) — and size modifiers.
- **Events**: none by default; when a control property is bound, the renderer
  reports `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` / `MEDIA_ENDED` /
  `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` (see EVENTS.md).
- **Renderer mapping**: GTK `GtkMediaFile`/GStreamer; HTML `<audio controls>`
  when there are no children, else a hidden `<audio>` + the children.

### Video — `VIDEO` 0x0A

A video playback node. Playback is **renderer-native by default** (`controls`);
a custom `VideoStyle` supplies app-driven control children, mirroring `AUDIO`.

- **Protocol**: a leaf node by default; source via `VIDEO_SOURCE` (0x1034,
  STRING asset reference). Custom style → children = the control UI.
- **Properties**: `VIDEO_SOURCE`, `CONTENT_MODE`, the media control properties
  (`PLAYBACK_STATE`, `MEDIA_POSITION`, `MEDIA_VOLUME`), size modifiers.
- **Events**: none by default; the media events above when a control property
  is bound.
- **Renderer mapping**: GTK `GtkVideo`/`GtkMediaFile`; HTML `<video controls>`
  when there are no children, else a hidden `<video>` + the children.
- **Note**: a poster/preview frame is a planned draft (`POSTER_SOURCE`); a
  video plays fine without one.

content.text:
I've traced the bug. Here's the diagnosis and fix plan.

## Root cause: a seek-echo loop locks the player paused

The flow that breaks (in `lib/typescript/src/apply.ts`):

1. Click **play** → `playing.set(true)` → `SET_PROPERTY(PLAYBACK_STATE=1)` over the WS → client `media.play()`.
2. The audio starts, `timeupdate` fires → client sends `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED(0.1)`.
3. The app writes `position.set(0.1)` — **but `position` is the same State bound to the media node's `MEDIA_POSITION`** — so the emitter re-emits `MEDIA_POSITION=0.1` → client `applyMediaProperty` does `media.currentTime = 0.1`.
4. That seek (a split-second in, while the source is still buffering) interrupts the just-started playback → the element fires `pause`.
5. The client's `pause` listener (past the 100 ms suppression) sends `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED(0)` → app sets `playing=false` → re-emits `PLAYBACK_STATE=0` → client `pause()`.
6. **Locked paused.** Every subsequent play click repeats the cycle → "plays a tiny split second then stops," and the stuck state persists.

## Fix plan (DOM client — `lib/typescript/src/apply.ts`)

1. **Guard the seek** (`applyMediaProperty`, `MEDIA_POSITION`): only set `media.currentTime` when the media is ready (`readyState >= HAVE_METADATA`) **and** the delta is meaningful (`|currentTime − target| > 0.25 s`); apply the 250 ms `timeupdate` suppression only after a *real* seek. This makes the timeupdate→`MEDIA_POSITION` echo a no-op during playback, so it can't interrupt the audio.
2. **Report play/pause/volume only for user-driven media**: attach the `play`/`pause`/`volumechange` reporters only when the media has native `controls` (the only case where a user can drive them). App-driven custom-control media never echoes play/pause/volume — breaking the pause lock at the source. Keep `timeupdate` (report only while `!media.paused`) and `ended`.
3. **Rebuild** `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` and re-copy into both demo modules.

Autoplay policy is likely *not* the blocker (the click grants transient page activation, and the WS round-trip is within it — consistent with the brief play you saw), so the echo fix should fully resolve it.

## Optional deeper fix (if the client guard proves insufficient)

Split the demo's *seek* from its *display* position (a `WritableSignal` the seek slider writes, separate from a read-only progress State the `timeupdate` events update) so `MEDIA_POSITION` re-emits only on a real user drag. Fully decouples progress display from seeks — a DSL/demo change, deferred unless needed.

Want me to proceed with the client fixes (steps 1–3)?

The fix is in place. Summary:

## Playback bug fixed — no more split-second stop

**Root cause** (as diagnosed): clicking play started the audio, but the first `timeupdate` → `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` → the app's `position` State → re-emitted `MEDIA_POSITION` → the DOM client set `media.currentTime` back to a near-identical value. That near-no-op seek interrupted the just-started playback (fired `pause`), and the client's `pause` echo → `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED(0)` → the app set `playing=false` → re-emitted `PLAYBACK_STATE=0` → client `pause()` — locking the player in the stuck state that repeated on every play click.

**Changes in `lib/typescript/src/apply.ts`:**
1. **Seek guard** — `MEDIA_POSITION` only sets `media.currentTime` when the change is meaningful (`|currentTime − target| > 0.25 s`), with the 250 ms `timeupdate` suppression only after a real seek. The timeupdate echo is now a no-op, so it can't interrupt playback.
2. **No play/pause/volume echo for app-driven media** — those listeners now attach only when the media has native `controls` (the only case a user drives them directly). Custom-control media never echoes them, breaking the pause lock at the source. `timeupdate` (only while `!media.paused`) and `ended` are always reported, so progress + auto-advance still work.

**Verified:** new unit test (`seeks only on a meaningful MEDIA_POSITION change`) — 173 TS tests + typecheck green; bundle rebuilt and copied into both demo modules; Spring demo jar rebuilt; served page + audio asset confirmed.

I found good sources. Here's the plan.

## Plan: real free music + real cover images

### Music (replace the 6 SoundHelix tracks)
Two reliable, legitimately-free options:

- **Chosic.com (CC0 / public domain, no attribution)** — real tracks by real artists (John Bartmann, Loyalty Freak Music, etc.) across many genres: **folk, country-ish, blues, jazz, celtic, acoustic, cinematic, pop**. Direct download links (`chosic.com/download-audio/<id>/`). This gives *modern-sounding* real songs with variety ("Country etc.? Anything?" → I'd pick a 2-genre mix, e.g. folk/acoustic + blues/jazz). Downloadable via curl (I'll verify the endpoint returns an mp3 at execution).
- **archive.org public-domain 78rpm collections** — authentic old-time country/jazz/blues (pre-1928, Public Domain Mark). Definitely free, stable `archive.org/download/<id>/<file>` URLs — but old 78rpm fidelity.

I'd recommend **Chosic CC0** for the best "real songs, modern feel" result (and it stays mono-64k re-encoded, so repo size stays ~16 MB). If Chosic's download is script-gated, I'll fall back to archive.org.

### Cover images (replace the 2 gradient SVGs)
**picsum.photos** — real photographs, free to use, deterministic via seed:
- `https://picsum.photos/seed/neon-nights/600/600` → `cover1.jpg`
- `https://picsum.photos/seed/blue-hour/600/600` → `cover2.jpg`
Downloaded as JPGs into both demo modules, referenced by the updated `Track.cover` paths.

### Steps
1. Download 6 CC0 tracks (Chosic) → re-encode mono 64k → `track1..6.mp3` in both modules (verify each with `ffprobe`; set `Track.duration` to real lengths).
2. Download 2 picsum photos → `cover1/2.jpg` in both modules.
3. Update `MusicPlayerView.TRACKS` (`audio`/`cover`/`duration`) + remove the old `cover*.svg` (or keep if you want a third album later).
4. Tests + clean-repack Spring jar; verify served assets + durations.
5. Commit.

content.text:
Confirmed both bugs. Here's the diagnosis and plan.

## Root cause

**1. Position not reset on skip** — `PlayerControlsStyle.prev()/next()` only call `trackIndex.update(...)`; they never reset `position` to 0 (only `PlayerBar.ended()` does). So the new song's progress/seek bar shows the old position mapped onto the new song.

**2. Doesn't auto-play on skip while playing** — changing `audio.src` resets the media element to a paused/loading state at 0. Since `playing` doesn't change on a skip, no `PLAYBACK_STATE` re-emit reaches the DOM client, so it never calls `play()` again. (`ended()` only works because it toggles `playing` false→true to force a re-emit — prev/next don't.)

## Fix plan

**Demo** (`PlayerControlsStyle.java`) — reset position on skip:
- Change the ⏮/⏭ button actions from `this::prev`/`this::next` to lambdas that also do `config.position().set(0f)`.

**Demo** (`PlayerBar.java`) — simplify `ended()`: drop the `playing.set(false); playing.set(true)` toggle (now unnecessary once the client resumes on source change); keep `trackIndex.update` + `position.set(0)`.

**Client** (`lib/typescript/src/apply.ts`) — resume playback on a source change when the app is playing:
- `mediaState` entries gain `playing: boolean` (default false); `applyMediaProperty` records it when `PLAYBACK_STATE` is applied.
- New `resumeIfPlaying(el)`: if the media's `state.playing` is true, call `media.play()` (swallow the promise rejection — transient not-ready/autoplay).
- Call it in the `AUDIO_SOURCE`/`VIDEO_SOURCE` branch of `applyStyle`, right after the source is applied.

**Tests + verify**
- TS: extend the media apply test — apply `PLAYBACK_STATE=1`, then change `AUDIO_SOURCE`, and assert `play()` is invoked (spy; adjust if happy-dom's media stubs differ).
- Rebuild `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` + copy into both demos; rebuild demo-views + clean-repack the Spring jar.
- Run the demo: skipping next/prev while playing resets progress to 0 and keeps playing (no pause needed).

Go?

content.text:
I've traced the root cause. Here's the diagnosis and plan.

## Root cause

`Audio.render`/`Video.render` do `node.component = Components.AUDIO/VIDEO`, **overwriting the custom style body's component**. So `PlayerControlsStyle.makeBody` returns a `VStack` node, but `Audio.render` forces it to `AUDIO` — the renderer then emits the media wrapper (block, no flex) instead of a `VStack`, and the debug comment says `Audio`. The `VStack`'s `display:flex;flex-direction:column` is lost (so the `Spacer`/seek-pin-to-bottom doesn't work), and the layout/comment don't match the authoring.

## Fix plan — preserve the style body's component

**1. Java DSL** (`Audio.java`/`Video.java`): remove `node.component = Components.AUDIO/VIDEO`. The style body decides the component:
- `NativeAudioStyle`/`NativeVideoStyle`'s `MediaBody` already returns `new PathlandNode(Components.AUDIO/VIDEO)` → native `<audio controls>`.
- A custom style returns its container (e.g. `VStack`) → component `VSTACK`.

**2. `pathland-render-html`**: a node carrying `AUDIO_SOURCE`/`VIDEO_SOURCE` **with children** (an app-driven custom-media container) now renders as its container (e.g. a flex-column `VStack`) with a hidden control-less `<audio src … data-pathland-media></audio>` prepended to the children, and the `data-pathland-media` marker on the container (so the DOM client wires playback events). `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` components with **no** children keep the native `<audio/video controls>`; keep a defensive wrapper branch for an AUDIO-with-children node. Remove the now-unneeded `.pathland-media` hide-CSS (a control-less `<audio>` is inherently invisible).

**3. TS client** (`apply.ts`): add `ensureMediaElement(el, propId)` that injects a hidden `<audio>`/`<video>` into a media **container** that doesn't yet have one; call it in the `AUDIO_SOURCE`/`VIDEO_SOURCE` apply path and in `applyMediaProperty` (so play/pause/seek/source work on a live-created container too). Broaden `finalizeNativeMedia` to the plain-container case. `mediaElementOf`/`setupMediaElement`/`resumeIfPlaying` already find the inner media via `querySelector`, so hydration + listeners keep working. `index.ts`'s `[data-pathland-media]` boot wiring still matches the container.

**4. Tests**:
- Rewrite the render-html custom-controls test to the container model: a `VSTACK` + `AUDIO_SOURCE` + child → flex column, hidden `<audio>`, `data-pathland-media` marker, `VStack` debug comment.
- `MusicPlayerViewTest`: the media node is now `VSTACK` — drop the `countCreate(Components.AUDIO)==1` assertion (the `AUDIO_SOURCE` property assertion already covers it).
- ssr-conformance native media fixture unchanged.

**5. Verify**: `cargo test` (render-html + golden), TS typecheck/tests, rebuild `dist` + copy, `mvn install`, clean-repack Spring jar — the served bar should now be a flex-column `VStack` (`display:flex;flex-direction:column`, debug `VStack`), seek bar pinned to the bottom.

No protocol/spec changes — purely renderer/DSL/client structure. Go?

## Done — the media bar now renders as a real VStack

**Root cause**: `Audio.render`/`Video.render` overwrote the custom style body's component with `AUDIO`, so `PlayerControlsStyle.makeBody`'s `VStack` was rendered as a media wrapper (block, no flex, "Audio" debug comment) instead of a `VStack`.

- **TS client**: added `ensureMediaElement` (creates the hidden media in a live-created container) and wired it into the source + media-property apply paths; `setupMediaElement`/`resumeIfPlaying` find it via `querySelector`.
- Tests: render-html custom-controls test rewritten for the container model (asserts `display:flex;flex-direction:column`, the hidden `<audio>`, the marker, and the `VStack` debug comment); `MusicPlayerViewTest` updated (media node is now a `VSTACK`).

## Important Details
- Branch: `feat/music-player-demo` (HTML-only Java demo; Qt/GTK out of scope).
- Root cause: `Audio.render`/`Video.render` did `node.component = Components.AUDIO/VIDEO`, clobbering the style body's component (VSTACK) → renderer emitted the media wrapper (block, no flex) + "Audio" debug comment, breaking the seek-pin/Spacer layout.

content.text:
## Root cause found

The Spring Boot demo serves the audio from **inside the jar** (classpath). Its static handler ignores `Range` headers for classpath resources:

```
$ curl -H "Range: bytes=1000000-1004095" /_pathland/assets/audio/track1.mp3
HTTP/1.1 200                 ← must be 206 Partial Content
Content-Length: 1658542      ← full body, no Content-Range / Accept-Ranges
```

When you seek the slider to a position beyond what the browser has buffered, the `<audio>` element issues a byte-range request. A `200` full-body reply to a range request makes browsers treat it as a fresh resource and **reset the media to byte 0** — the track restarts from the beginning. (Durations themselves match the files, the emitter only re-sends `MEDIA_POSITION` on a seek, and the client's 0.25s seek-guard is fine — I ruled those out.)

I couldn't get the Quarkus app to boot in my quick test, but its vertx static handler natively serves classpath resources with `206`, so this is likely Spring-only.

## Proposed fix (Spring demo)

Make `/_pathland/**` range-capable by serving it from a real filesystem directory instead of the jar:

1. New `@Configuration` (`MediaRangeConfig` implements `WebMvcConfigurer`) in `pathland-spring-boot-demo`:
   - **Extract on startup**: use Spring's `PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver("classpath:/static/_pathland/**")` to copy the demo's media assets (6 mp3s, 2 covers, dom-renderer.js ≈ 10 MB) into a stable runtime dir (e.g. `java.io.tmpdir/pathland-media/<content-hash>/`), guarded by a marker file so restarts don't re-copy.
   - **Register a resource handler**: `registry.addResourceHandler("/_pathland/**").addResourceLocations(fileDir.toUri())` — the more specific pattern wins over the default `/**`, and Spring's `FileSystemResource` serving emits proper `206 Partial Content` + `Content-Range`.
2. Keeps the jar self-contained and the run instructions unchanged.

Verification: rebuild + run the jar; `curl -H "Range: bytes=1000000-1004095"` must return `206`; then browser-test that seeking no longer restarts the track. Also verify the Quarkus demo already returns `206` (no change expected).

Alternative (if you'd rather avoid startup file writes): a small `@RestController` for `/_pathland/assets/audio/*` that parses `Range` via Spring's `HttpRange` and returns `ResponseEntity<ResourceRegion>` (206). ~30 lines, but hand-rolled for single ranges and audio-only.

Two questions before I implement:

Plan finalized.

## Plan: fix media seeking (tracks restarting) via byte-range support

**Cause**: media served from inside the jar; Spring/classpath static serving answers `Range` with a full `200`, so a browser seek beyond the buffer restarts the `<audio>` at byte 0.

### 1. Spring demo — extract + file resource handler
New `MediaRangeConfig` (`@Configuration implements WebMvcConfigurer`) in `pathland-spring-boot-demo`:
- **Startup extract**: enumerate `classpath:/static/_pathland/**` via `PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver` and copy the assets (6 mp3s, 2 covers, dom-renderer.js) into a stable runtime dir — `java.io.tmpdir/pathland-media/<sha256-of-asset-manifest>/` — guarded by a matching manifest file so restarts skip the copy.
- **Handler**: `registry.addResourceHandler("/_pathland/**").addResourceLocations(fileDir.toUri().toString())`. The more specific pattern beats the default `/** → classpath:/static/`, and real files give Spring's native `206 Partial Content` + `Content-Range` (incl. multi-range/If-Range).
- Self-contained jar and run commands unchanged.

### 2. Quarkus demo — verify, align if needed
- Boot `pathland-quarkus-demo` (it failed to start within my quick wait — needs more startup time), then `curl -H "Range: bytes=…"` the audio → expect `206` from vertx's `StaticHandler`. If it already returns `206`: no code change (just confirm). If `200`: apply an analogous fix (extract to a dir + vertx `StaticHandler.create()` route on `/_pathland/*`, or extract-and-serve via the same strategy).

### 3. Verify
- Rebuild both jars (`mvn clean package -DskipTests`), run each, confirm `Range` → `206` + `Content-Range` on a mid-file byte range.
- Browser-test on both: seek the slider forward while playing → track stays at the sought position (no restart).
- No protocol/opcode/TS changes; no `status.md` updates expected (demo infra only).

Ready to implement on your go-ahead.

content.text:
Done. The seek bug was a serving issue, not protocol.

**Root cause**: `PathlandIndexController.framework()` served every `/_pathland/**` asset (audio included) from the classpath by streaming the full bytes as `200`, ignoring `Range` headers. When you drag the seek slider past the buffered region, the `<audio>` sends a byte-range request — a full `200` in reply makes browsers reset the media resource to byte 0, restarting the track.

**Fix** (`b66e2aa7`): the shared starter's controller now honors a `Range` request with `206 Partial Content` + `Content-Range`, advertises `Accept-Ranges` on full responses, and returns `416` for unsatisfiable ranges — at both the global and per-mount (`/app2`) bases.

**Verified**:
- `Range: bytes=1000000-1004095` → `206`, `Content-Range: bytes 1000000-1004095/1658542`, and the returned bytes match the jar entry exactly.
- Suffix (`bytes=-500`) and open-ended (`bytes=1000000-`) ranges → `206`; out-of-range → `416`.
- Quarkus already serves these classpath assets with `206` via its vertx static handler — no change needed there (confirmed).
- Full `mvn install` (all Java tests) green; SSR page unchanged.

One detour: I first tried extracting assets to a file dir and registering a resource handler, but the starter's `@GetMapping("/_pathland/**")` controller outranks resource handlers — fixing the controller was the correct spot.

`wid` = **window id** — a per-browser-tab identifier that scopes the app's *persisted state* on the server, so two windows/tabs of the same app never share state (and a reload of the same tab keeps its state).

**How it flows** (`lib/typescript/src/index.ts:119-160`):
1. The DOM client generates a UUID on first visit, stores it in `sessionStorage` under `pathland.wid`, and reflects it into the URL via `history.replaceState` (`?wid=<uuid>`).
2. It's sent to the server on the **WebSocket URL** (`/ws?wid=…`) and, because it lives in the URL, on every **SSR request** (page load/reload).

**Server side** (`PathlandSocket.java:95-97`, `PathlandRegistry`):
- Each WS connection still gets a **fresh `uiId`** — its own UI model (retained tree + emitter instance).
- The `wid` is the **state scope**: `PersistentState` keys entries as `name:scope` (the wid), so the player's `position`/`playing`/`trackIndex`/`volume` are per-window.

**Why it matters**:
- **Same-tab reload**: `sessionStorage` keeps the wid → the reload's SSR request carries `?wid=` → the HTML is rendered *with* that window's latest state — no resync.
- **New tab/window**: fresh `sessionStorage` → new wid → SSR renders defaults. If a same-tab reload's URL somehow lost the wid (typed URL), the client requests a `META::RESYNC` on connect to restore the window's persisted state (`isReload && !urlHasWid`).

content.text:
Short answer: **yes, mechanically it could — but it would change a documented design decision.** The `wid` isn't a user session; it's a *per-window* scope, and a cookie can't express "per tab."

## What `wid` actually is
`wid` = the **persisted-state scope**: `PersistentState` keys are `name:<scope>` where scope = `mount:windowId` (`PathlandRegistry.java:92`). It exists so **two tabs never share state** — an explicit, repeated design goal ("SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS)", `PathlandRegistry.java:123`). It's carried in the URL and on the WS query so a **same-tab reload** renders the latest state with no resync.

## Why a cookie changes the semantics
Cookies are **per-origin**, not per-tab — every tab of the browser shares one cookie value. So:
- A session cookie would collapse **all tabs into one state scope**: two windows would share `position`/`playing`/`trackIndex`/`volume` and fight over the slider.
- The per-connection UI model would *still* be isolated (that's the fresh `uiId`), but the state wouldn't be.

So the real question is a product choice: keep per-tab isolation, or switch to tab-sharing.

## What a cookie would buy you (if you want tab-sharing)
- No URL pollution (wid leaves the address bar/history/referrer/logs), no `history.replaceState`, no `sessionStorage` dance, and the `isReload && !urlHasWid` RESYNC special-case disappears — the server just reads `Set-Cookie`/`Cookie` on the SSR request and the WS handshake (browsers attach cookies to same-origin WS upgrades).
- Server-side generation (set the cookie itself) rather than trusting a client UUID.

## What it costs
1. **Loses per-window isolation** (the whole point of `wid`).
2. Reverses a documented decision → spec/DSL docs + `status.md` updates.
3. Cookie etiquette (SameSite, `Secure`, size) becomes part of the contract.

## If you *want* to keep isolation but lose the URL leak
A middle path: drop `wid` from the page URL, keep it only on the WS. Then every reload SSR's **defaults** and the client issues a `META::RESYNC` on connect (exactly today's `!urlHasWid` path) — simpler URL, at the cost of a defaults-flash + one full snapshot per reload. The URL-wid is load-bearing for "reload paints the latest state instantly."

Which behavior do you actually want — **keep per-tab isolation** (current), **share state across tabs via a session cookie**, or **isolated but with the id kept out of the URL** (defaults + RESYNC per reload)?
Is there no way to get a identification of the window without polluting url?

No — not for free. The constraint is fundamental: the SSR request is a **plain navigation GET that runs before any page JS**. A navigation GET can only carry information via the **URL**, **cookies**, or **headers** — and there is no per-tab channel among them:

- **Cookies are per-origin**, not per-tab. Every tab reads the same cookie, so a cookie can't encode "which window" — and if tab A overwrote it with its own id, tab B's reload would inherit tab A's id. A per-tab cookie is impossible.
- **Headers** on a navigation can't be set by JS.
- **The URL fragment** (`#wid`) isn't sent to the server at all — dead end.

sessionStorage is the *only* per-tab storage, and it's invisible to the server until JS runs — i.e., after SSR. So the id must ride a request the page's JS controls (the WebSocket) — which means **instant SSR of the right window's state and a clean URL are mutually exclusive**, *unless* you add a service worker. Concretely:

**Option A — current (`?wid=` in URL).** Reload SSR paints the latest state instantly, no flash, no resync. Cost: wid lives in the address bar/history/referrer/logs.

**Option B — sessionStorage + WS query only, no page-URL wid.** The id survives reloads in sessionStorage and travels only on the WS handshake (`ws://…/ws?wid=…`, which is internal, not the page URL). SSR always renders defaults; the client already has the `isReload && !urlHasWid → META::RESYNC` path (`lib/typescript/src/index.ts:152-159`), and the server's session loads persisted state from the WS's scope and RESYNCs it — so the correct window state is restored. **Cost: every reload flashes defaults then applies a full snapshot.** This is a small change (stop the `replaceState`), and the architecture already supports it.

**Option C — service worker rewrites the navigation** (append `?wid=` or set a header invisibly before it hits the network). Clean address bar **and** instant SSR. Cost: SW registration (first visit has none), lifecycle/complexity, HTTPS/localhost-only. Real technique, but heavy for a framework's baseline.

**Option D — session cookie.** Clean URL, but collapses all tabs into one shared state scope — it fixes pollution by *dropping per-tab isolation*, which contradicts the documented design.

My recommendation: **Option B** — it's the honest answer to "no URL pollution" with per-window isolation, and it's ~half-wired already. Choose **C** only if "reload must paint the saved state with no defaults flash" is a hard requirement.

Which do you want to pursue?
With option B, a brand new session would not need to apply a snapshot, would it?

Exactly right. In Option B the snapshot fires **only** when `sessionStorage` already holds a wid — i.e. a same-tab reload. A brand-new session needs nothing:

- **Fresh visit (new tab)**: `sessionStorage` is empty → `isReload = false` → no RESYNC is sent (`lib/typescript/src/index.ts:156`). The SSR renders defaults, and the fresh WS session mounts a brand-new tree with a brand-new scope (the just-generated wid) — also defaults. Identical, nothing to restore.

- **Same-tab reload**: `isReload = true`, and (under Option B) the URL never carries a wid, so the client requests a full snapshot. The snapshot is what restores that window's **persisted** state: the WS session's scope comes from the sessionStorage wid, so its `PersistentState` re-loads the saved `position`/`playing`/`trackIndex`/`volume` at mount, and the RESYNC delivers that tree.

So the snapshot is purely the "reload-restores-saved-state" mechanism — fresh sessions never pay for it. The only cost on a reload is the defaults-flash + one full snapshot (~the size of the tree), which is the tradeoff Option B trades for a clean URL.

If you want to soften the flash, a follow-up tweak (still Option B) is for the SSR to render a neutral shell when there's no `wid` on the request, instead of a wrong-but-plausible default UI. Want me to fold that into the plan?

content.text:
Right — let me explain what that follow-up actually entails, because I glossed over an important mechanism constraint.

## The flash under Option B
On a same-tab reload (no wid in URL), the SSR always renders **defaults**, then the client RESYNCs the saved state. So you'd briefly see e.g. "Fiddles McGinty · 0:00" flash before "OctoBlues · 2:41" lands. The follow-up was: render a **neutral shell** instead, so nothing *false* flashes.

## The constraint I need to own up to
The SSR tree and the WebSocket session's mount frame must be the **same tree** (same node ids). The server deliberately does *not* send the mount frame — `PathlandSession` assumes the client's tree equals its own ("Only deltas + resync snapshots go out"). This is what makes the fast paths work:

- **Fresh visit**: SSR renders defaults (default scope); session mounts with the fresh wid scope (also defaults). Same tree → match → **no snapshot** — exactly your point, confirmed.
- **Same-tab reload**: SSR renders defaults (default scope); session mounts with the *saved* wid scope → loads persisted state → **different tree** → the client MUST resync to converge.

So a shell only preserves the fast paths if it's the **same skeleton with the same ids**, just *blank values*. A different-shaped "loading UI" would make the client unable to treat the SSR tree as the live tree — forcing a RESYNC on **every** load, including fresh visits. That would throw away the "brand-new session needs no snapshot" property you just confirmed.

## Why I now recommend skipping the server-side shell
To get a same-skeleton-but-blank shell, the server would need a "render with blanked state" mode, and "blank" is app-specific (empty library, no selection, no position) — real complexity for a cosmetic win that's sub-second anyway. Not worth it.

**Better follow-up (client-only, zero server change):** the client already knows on `isReload` that it will RESYNC. It can simply hold painting — show a lightweight "restoring…" placeholder over the SSR defaults until the snapshot hydrates. All fast paths (fresh visit: no snapshot) stay intact.

## Refined plan
1. **TS client** (`lib/typescript/src/index.ts`): stop reflecting wid into the page URL (`history.replaceState` block) — wid lives only in `sessionStorage` + the WS query. On connect, RESYNC when `isReload` (sessionStorage wid present). Optionally: hold/replace the SSR content with a "restoring…" overlay during the reload resync.
2. **Server**: no change needed — the RESYNC path and scope handling already work; SSR keeps rendering defaults when no wid is present.
3. **Java `stateScope`**: unchanged; scope still keyed by the WS's wid.
4. Update `status.md`/docs that describe the URL-wid behavior.
5. Verify: fresh tab → no snapshot (only deltas); same-tab reload → one RESYNC restoring saved state; two tabs remain isolated; address bar stays clean.

Want me to proceed with **Option B + the client-side hold**, or Option B without the hold?
B without the hold

Confirmed the full picture. `index.ts:193`'s route-mirror reuses `urlParams` captured at boot, so stripping `wid` there keeps the address bar clean across navigations too.

## Plan: Option B — per-window id without URL pollution (no hold)

**Behavior after this change:** the `wid` lives only in `sessionStorage` + the WebSocket URL (internal, never the page URL). A fresh visit needs no snapshot (SSR defaults == fresh session defaults). A same-tab reload (or any load whose URL carries a stale `wid`) SSR-renders defaults and the client requests one `META::RESYNC` to restore the window's persisted state.

### 1. `lib/typescript/src/index.ts` (~lines 119–160)
- Delete the `history.replaceState(..., "?wid=…")` reflection block.
- Instead: capture `urlHadWid = urlParams.has("wid")`; if present, `urlParams.delete("wid")` and `replaceState` without it (guarding the empty-search `?`), so bookmarked/shared `?wid=` URLs from the pre-migration build get cleaned and the route-mirror closure stays clean.
- Change the connect-time resync condition from `isReload && !urlHasWid` to `isReload || urlHadWid` (resync whenever the SSR's scope could differ from the session's).
- Update the surrounding comments (per-window identity, no URL reflection, resync on reload).

### 2. `lib/typescript/test/wid.test.ts` (rewrite to new semantics)
- Fresh window: wid in `sessionStorage` + WS URL; **no** wid in page URL; no RESYNC (1 message).
- Same-tab reload (sessionStorage wid present): same wid on WS; RESYNC requested (2 messages).
- Load with a stale `?wid=` in the URL: wid stripped from the address bar + RESYNC requested.
- Mounted-app route mirror: pushes `/app2/home` with **no** wid in the URL.
- Two windows → different wids (unchanged).

### 3. Docs/status (`AGENTS.md` + status.md + javadoc)
- `lib/typescript/status.md` (per-window identity bullet, ~17–24).
- `lib/java/pathland-server-core/status.md` (~34–40: "client reflects the wid into the page URL … no resync" → new behavior).
- `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/status.md` (~20: wid now only on the WS `?wid=`, not the SSR request).
- `PathlandIndexController.java` + `PathlandRegistry.java` javadoc that describe the URL reflection; check `pathland-quarkus-starter/status.md` for the same phrasing.
- `AGENTS.md` lib/typescript bullet: "full snapshot … after reconnect" → "after a reconnect or a same-tab reload".

### 4. Build & verify
- `npm run typecheck` + `npm test` (updated `wid.test.ts` green).
- `npm run build:all` (rebuilds `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js`, copies into both demo modules).
- Repack both demo jars (`mvn -pl pathland-spring-boot-demo -pl pathland-quarkus-demo clean package -DskipTests`).
- Manual smoke on Spring (and spot-check Quarkus): fresh tab → no snapshot; same-tab reload → exactly one RESYNC restoring saved state (no defaults flash of the old tree, per "no hold"); two tabs stay isolated; address bar never shows `?wid=`.

**No server code changes** — the server already renders defaults when the SSR request lacks a `wid` and scopes each WS session by the WS `wid`.

Committed as `4208eaff`. Option B is in — the `wid` now lives only in `sessionStorage` + the WS URL, never the page URL.

**What changed:**
- **`index.ts`**: removed the `history.replaceState(…?wid=…)` reflection; instead strips any stale `?wid=` from the address bar (preserving other params, keeping the route-mirror closure clean); resync condition is now `isReload || urlHadWid`.
- **`wid.test.ts`** rewritten: fresh window → no URL wid, no RESYNC; same-tab reload → same wid on WS + exactly one RESYNC; stale-URL wid → stripped + RESYNC; route mirror → clean URL; two windows → distinct wids.
- **Docs/status/javadoc**: `lib/typescript/status.md`, `pathland-server-core/status.md`, `pathland-spring-boot-starter/status.md`, `PathlandRegistry`/`PathlandIndexController` javadoc, `AGENTS.md`.

**No server code changes** — `renderHtml` with no wid already renders defaults; the WS wid still scopes `PersistentState`.

**Verified**: `tsc` + 174 TS tests green, `mvn install` green, bundle rebuilt + copied into both demos, jars repacked; Spring demo serves with the new bundle (`ws?wid=`, `has("wid")`/`delete("wid")` present), and the byte-range fix still returns `206`.

The one behavioral cost of Option B (as agreed): a same-tab reload SSR-renders defaults, then applies one full RESYNC snapshot to restore the window's state — no hold/overlay, just the swap.

# pathland-render-gtk — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 14, 2026

The **GTK4 renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto native GTK widgets
(shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`. Design-token contract:
`spec/TOKENS.md`.

## Implemented

- **Components → widgets** (`widget_kind`/`build_widget`):
  - `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` → `GtkBox` (spacing/alignment/
    padding/content-margins),
  - `TEXT` → `GtkLabel` (text, `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`COLOR` via Pango),
  - `BUTTON` → `GtkButton` (label; composite body when it has children),
  - `GRID`/`LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` → `GtkGrid` (row-major cells from child
    index + `WIDTH` column count),
  - `SCROLLVIEW` → `GtkScrolledWindow` (single child),
  - `ZSTACK` → `GtkOverlay`,
  - `SPACER` → expanding box, `IMAGE` → `GtkPicture` (`IMAGE_SOURCE`),
  - `TOGGLE` → `GtkSwitch`/`GtkCheckButton`/`GtkToggleButton` by `TOGGLE_STYLE`
    (`SELECTED` ↔ active),
  - `SLIDER` → `GtkScale` (`VALUE`/`MIN`/`MAX`/`STEP`),
  - `TEXT_FIELD` → `GtkEntry` (`LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`IS_SECURE`),
  - `TEXT_EDITOR` → `GtkTextView` (multi-line),
  - `COLOR` → `GtkDrawingArea` (solid fill), `SHAPE` → `GtkDrawingArea`
    (`SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER` → `GtkSeparator`,
  - `PROGRESS_VIEW` → `GtkProgressBar`/`GtkSpinner`,
  - `GAUGE` → `GtkLevelBar`, `STEPPER` → `GtkSpinButton`,
  - `DATE_PICKER` → `GtkCalendar`, `PICKER` → `GtkDropDown` (option children +
    `SELECTION`), `MENU` → `GtkMenuButton`, `COLOR_PICKER` → `GtkColorButton`.
  Unknown components → blank `GtkLabel`.
- **Container + composite reconciliation** (diff-guarded): stacks/grid/scroll/
  overlay children, and **Composite Override Mode** for `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`MENU`
  with children (custom body wrapped in the native button shell).
- **Style properties**: `VISIBLE`, `OPACITY`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`,
  `CONTENT_MARGINS`, `PADDING` + per-edge, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_WIDTH`/
  `COLOR`/`RADIUS`, `FONT_FAMILY`/`FONT_WEIGHT` (CSS provider), `COLOR`,
  `FONT_SIZE`.
- **`FILL` expansion**: a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` of `FILL` (-1.0, SwiftUI
  `maxWidth/maxHeight: .infinity`) now sets `hexpand`/`vexpand` + `Fill` axis
  alignment so arbitrary elements truly expand to the available space; a finite
  value is a size request and `HUG_CONTENT` leaves the natural size.
- **Events**: pointer `POINTER_DOWN`/`MOVE`/`UP` via `GestureClick`/
  `EventControllerMotion` (`EVENT_LISTENERS`-driven), plus **value/text events**
  (`VALUE_CHANGED` from toggle/slider/picker, `TEXT_CHANGED` from text field)
  **gated by `BINDING_ID`** (transport-aware event guards), sent through the
  two-way event arena.
- **Platform back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `EventControllerKey`
  (capture phase, attached once in `run_with_pump`) maps Escape — and
  BackSpace when no text entry has focus — to `Event::Navigate { url: None }`
  through the shared event sink. `NAVIGATE` is global (never node-keyed),
  matching spec/EVENTS.md.
- **Native navigation slot (`AdwNavigationView`)**: a stack node carrying the
  `ROUTE` property (a `NavigationContainer`, spec/DSL.md §4.5) renders as an
  `AdwNavigationView` instead of a `GtkBox`. The adapter reconciles its page
  stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH` 0x201A, U32): it pops pages down to the
  app's depth, then **pushes** when the route is deeper (normal push / deep
  link), **replaces the top page** when the depth is unchanged and the route
  differs (a guard redirect / `replace()`), and **refreshes in place** when the
  visible page already shows the route (a signal update, or a re-emit after a
  user-initiated back). In the default chrome mode (`NAV_CHROME` 0x201B
  `PlatformDefault`, or missing) each page wraps the destination in a
  `ToolbarView` + `HeaderBar` (`show-back-button`) — the native top bar and
  back button; in `Custom` chrome mode (`Chrome.CUSTOM` → `NAV_CHROME=1`) the
  page child is the bare destination (the developer owns all nav UI). The
  header-bar back button's `popped` signal drops the
  page from the adapter's mirror and emits `Event::Navigate { url: None }`
  (suppressed during renderer-driven pops), so native back and Escape both flow
  into the app's `router.pop()`. The back-stack stays app-owned; the
  `AdwNavigationView` is only the renderer's rendered-output cache.
  `libadwaita` (0.7, `v1_4` feature) is a new native dependency.
- **Design tokens / theming (spec/TOKENS.md renderer contract)**:
  - `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides are stored (`host.rs`), base + `dark.*`
    split by path prefix; STRING-valued overrides resolve the value string from
    the arena.
  - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values record the token path
    (`HostNode::token_refs`) and **resolve at apply time** against the theme,
    the active scheme, and the parent-fallback chain into concrete
    `properties`/`strings` (`RenderTree::resolve_tokens`, reusing
    `pathland_core::tokens`).
  - **Tier-1 default tables** (light + dark) in `host.rs`
    (`concrete_default_tables`) — concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks,
    **enriched with GTK-native theme colors** (`tokens.rs`:
    `StyleContext::lookup_color` of `@theme_*`/`@borders`/`@success_color`…)
    from the first widget's style context (headless → concrete fallback).
  - **Scheme detection** from the native GTK variant
    (`gtk::Settings` `prefer-dark` + `-dark` theme name); a notify handler
    calls `GtkRenderer::set_scheme`, which re-enriches native defaults and
    re-resolves + re-applies every token-referencing widget. Scheme is never
    carried by the protocol.
  - The generative `space.<N>` family resolves `space.base` × N.
  - Since GTK CSS has no custom properties, tokens resolve to **concrete**
    values (rgba/px/Pango) before the existing CSS-provider / text-style paths.
- **C ABI for foreign hosts (`capi.rs`)**:
  - `pathland_gtk_run(host, on_event)` — pump a `pathland-view-native`
    `NativeHost`'s ring in-process.
  - `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` — pump a
    **`libpathland_core` ring borrowed in-process** (from
    `pathland_core_ring_mut`): the route for hosts that emit opcodes themselves
    (the Java DSL writes into the ring via `RingOpcodeSink` and the renderer
    pumps the same ring in place — zero-copy, no `pathland-view-native` host).
    `width`/`height` size the default window.
  - Both block until the GTK main loop exits and share `run_with_pump_sized`
    (the 420×220 default lives in `run_with_pump`).
- **Robustness fixes (exercised by the Java `SplitNavDemo`, which uses controls
  the Rust demo never did)**:
  - **Slider step**: GTK's `gtk_scale_new_with_range` asserts a non-zero step;
    the renderer previously passed `0.0` unconditionally (a `SLIDER` crashed the
    process). A `STEP_VALUE` of 0 ("continuous" in the DSL) now derives a small
    increment (`(max-min)/100`, min `0.001`).
  - **Lazy stacks**: `LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` map to `WidgetKind::Stack`, but
    `stack_orientation` only accepted `VSTACK`/`HSTACK` — a lazy stack panicked
    at `stack_widget`. They now map to the same eager `GtkBox` orientations.
  - **Re-entrant control signals**: applying a frame borrows the pump
    zero-copy; a *programmatic* value change (e.g. `GtkScale::set_value`) fires
    the connected GTK signal synchronously and re-entered `emit`, double-borrowing
    the pump (`RefCell already borrowed`) and panicking. Such events are now
    **deferred to the idle pump** (`flush_pending` before each frame), which also
    prevents a control-echo loop when the host writes the same value back.

## Not implemented / gaps

- `SHAPE` `Path`/rounded rendering is an approximation (rectangle/circle fill).
- `MENU` renders a menu button without a popover item list.
- No `ACTION_ID`-only gating (events require `BINDING_ID`).
- Composite bodies attach to button-like controls only; other controls ignore
  children.
- `LAZY_*` renders eagerly (no GTK windowing).

**Last updated:** September 14, 2026

Runs the shared framework-agnostic demo views (`com.pathland.demo`, e.g.

cross-language, shared-renderer story for Java. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## How it works

- The Java DSL mounts the view through its fine-grained `Emitter` into a

- The in-process GTK renderer pumps the same ring in place

- Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains

  shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, router back).
- State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
  over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme, and

Good — I've mapped the full picture. Here's what "running the music player in the Java GTK demo" actually requires, in tiers.

## What already works (no change needed)
- **Java side is fully media-ready**: `pathland-core` has the `MediaPlayStateChanged`/`MediaTimeUpdated`/`MediaEnded`/`MediaVolumeChanged` events (`events.rs:107`), and the Java `FrameCodec` → `InputDispatcher` → `Audio.mediaInput` → signals path is wired (I verified it earlier for the web; it's transport-agnostic).
- **All components MusicPlayerView uses render under GTK**: VStack/HStack/Text/Button/Spacer/Image(`GtkPicture`)/Slider(`GtkScale`), ScrollView, Divider, plus the style props and `FILL` sizing — per `pathland-render-gtk/status.md`. `State` works too: `GtkHost` already provides a `PersistentState` (`InMemoryStateStore`, scope `"desktop"`), and the emitter already stamps `BINDING_ID` on bound controls so slider `VALUE_CHANGED` flows.
- `GtkHost` mounts the root view via the shared ring (`pathland_gtk_run_ring`) — swapping the root is a one-line change.

## The two gaps

**1. No AUDIO/VIDEO in the GTK renderer** — the real blocker. render-gtk has no media node handling, no media props (`PLAYBACK_STATE`/`MEDIA_POSITION`/`MEDIA_VOLUME`/`AUDIO_SOURCE`), and no media event emission. So on GTK the PlayerBar renders as its VStack body (buttons/sliders all live) but playback is inert: no sound, no `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED`, seek/volume/play don't stick.

**2. Asset paths are web URLs** — `MusicPlayerView` hardcodes `/_pathland/assets/…` (covers + mp3s). `GtkPicture.set_filename` and any file-based audio need local paths, so covers/audio won't resolve without a mapping.

## Tier 1 — music player *UI* on GTK (small)
- `GtkHost.main`: mount `new MusicPlayerView()` instead of `SplitNavDemo` (no router needed).
- Add a tiny asset-root resolution to render-gtk for `/_pathland/`-prefixed `IMAGE_SOURCE` (configurable via a new C ABI setter); `GtkHost` points it at a local covers dir.
- Result: the full Apple-Music-style layout on the desktop — library, sidebar, player bar, working sliders/buttons and reactive `State` — but **no sound** (playback props are no-ops).

## Tier 2 — real audio on GTK (the honest "running it")
Implement media in render-gtk using **`gtk::MediaFile`/`MediaStream`** (GStreamer-backed, ships inside GTK4 — no new C dependency; gtk4-rs 0.9 exposes it):
- AUDIO/VIDEO node (`AUDIO_SOURCE`/`VIDEO_SOURCE`): keep the custom AudioStyle's VStack body rendering (already works) and attach a hidden `GtkMediaFile`; map `PLAYBACK_STATE`→play/pause, `MEDIA_POSITION`→`seek`, `MEDIA_VOLUME`→volume; re-emitted `AUDIO_SOURCE` → reload + resume-if-playing.
- Emit `MEDIA_*` events back through the existing shared event ring (Rust `Event` variants + arena already exist). **Zero Java changes** — the dispatcher/mediaInput is ready.
- Asset-root setter for both images and audio; copy the mp3s/covers to a local dir for the demo.
- Tests in `pathland-render-gtk` (headless widget/media mapping) + manual run.

Tier 2 completes the desktop renderer's media story (the protocol contract already exists in `spec/EVENTS.md`) and gives the real "write once, play everywhere" demo.

**Suggested path: Tier 2.** The render-gtk media work is the substantive piece; Tier 1 is just its prerequisite UI swap.
