I have the facts I need. Here's the plan.

## Plan: Thorough per-component layout specs in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` (in place)

**Scope** (per your choice): sections A (drawing primitives) + B (layout containers). Spec-only; no renderer code changes. Each component's section grows a **"Layout & sizing"** subsection.

### Consistent format per component

1. **Size model** — the component's default size kind (greedy / Hug / Fixed-participant) + intrinsic-size rule, per `LAYOUT.md`.
2. **Sizing its content** — wrapping, `CONTENT_MODE` fit, aspect.
3. **In a container** — main/cross-axis behavior, spacing/alignment participation.
4. **Own sizing** — what its own `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` does (exact box, content fits inside).
5. **Overflow / clipping**.
6. **Cross-renderer mapping** — GTK4 / CSS / SwiftUI / Compose, one line each.
7. **Edge cases**.

### A. Drawing primitives — the layout rules I'll pin down

- **Text** — Hug both axes (natural size); a Fixed width wraps at native line breaks (`LINE_LIMIT`/`TRUNCATION_MODE` apply inside the box); never greedy; `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` aligns within the box.
- **Image** — natural size = intrinsic content points; Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` = exact box with `CONTENT_MODE` Fit/Fill inside (never upscales beyond the box); `ASPECT_RATIO`; absent size → intrinsic content.
- **Color** — greedy both axes (fills), Fixed box overrides (already partially documented — made precise).
- **Shape** — **greedy both axes by default** (SwiftUI semantics), Fixed box → exact box with geometry drawn inside. *(Found: render-html currently defaults `WIDTH/HEIGHT=100` — the spec will define greedy; status.md flags the divergence.)*
- **Divider** — greedy cross-axis, 1px main-axis; **orientation = parent's cross axis** (horizontal in a VStack, vertical in an HStack). *(Found: render-gtk always builds a `Horizontal` separator — status.md gap.)*
- **Spacer** — greedy main-axis, zero cross-axis content; no intrinsic size; explicit size overrides.
- **ProgressView** — determinate: main-axis greedy (fills available width, native bar default), natural height; indeterminate spinner: fixed natural size, never stretched.
- **Gauge** — main-axis greedy (fills available width — GTK `LevelBar`, CSS `width:100%`), natural height.

### B. Layout containers — exact allocation algorithms (the main deliverable)

Section B gets a **"Layout model" preamble** (Fixed/Fill/Hug, main/cross axis, greedy, `LAYOUT.md` reference), then per container:

- **VStack/HStack** — main-axis: Fixed exact / Fill expand (leftover **only** to Fill children) / Hug natural; cross-axis: children keep size, positioned by `ALIGNMENT` (default Leading), Fill children stretch; own size = hug (sum + spacing / widest) unless Fixed/Fill; `SPACING` gap (negative→0), `CONTENT_MARGINS` inset, `PADDING` margins. Mapping: `GtkBox` + per-child rule; CSS flex column/row, `align-items:flex-start` default.
- **ZStack** — depth overlay, later on top; container greedy both axes; children keep their size and are positioned by `ALIGNMENT`. *(Found: HTML wraps each child `position:absolute;inset:0`; GTK `GtkOverlay` main-child-fills but overlay alignment isn't set — status.md gap for GTK overlay positioning.)*
- **Grid** — 2D matrix; `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` = column/row count (`FILL`/absent = auto-fit); cells equal-size (`repeat(n,1fr)`); each child fills its cell unless Fixed (per `grid_cell_align`); `SPACING` = row/col gap.
- **ScrollView** — greedy both axes; first child is the content; viewport gives the child natural size on the scroll axis, fills the other; `overflow:auto`/automatic policies; `SCROLL`/`WHEEL` events.
- **Lazy variants** — identical allocation contract to the base stack/grid; **only realization is windowed** (off-screen children may be deferred). *(Note: render-gtk realizes eagerly — already in status.)*

### Status.md sync (AGENTS.md requirement)

Add gap notes to the affected projects' `status.md` for spec-defined behavior implementations currently diverge on (no code changes this pass):
- `pathland-render-html`: SHAPE default 100×100 vs greedy.
- `pathland-render-gtk`: Divider orientation (always horizontal) vs parent cross-axis; ZStack overlay alignment.

### Verification
- `cargo test` + `mvn install` unaffected (spec-only), but re-run to confirm nothing references removed text.
- Markdown lint pass (tables/links).

The ZStack default alignment in SwiftUI is **Center**, but our `LAYOUT.md` stack default is **Leading/Start**. I'll spec ZStack's default as **Center** (SwiftUI parity, and it's what both renderers' native behavior approximates) unless you'd rather keep it Leading/Start for consistency across all stacks. Focused plan for **VStack/HStack only**. I've verified the exact behavior in both renderers. Here's what will be written into `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` section B (replacing the current 4-line VStack/HStack entries).

## Plan: thorough `VStack`/`HStack` layout specs in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`

### 1. Rewrite the section B intro → "The stack layout model" preamble

A reusable preamble (so ZStack/Grid/ScrollView can reference it later) defining:
- **Size kinds** (Fixed = exact box / Fill = expand / Hug = natural) per `LAYOUT.md`.
- **Main axis** (layout direction) vs **cross axis**.
- The two stack rules: **main axis** — leftover goes only to `Fill` children (Fixed exact, Hug natural, everything else positioned at the start); **cross axis** — children keep their own size, `ALIGNMENT` positions (never resizes, default **Leading**, `Fill(3)` = default hug), `Fill` children stretch.
- A `Fill` child inside a **Hug** stack has no leftover to absorb → collapses to natural (bounded by the stack's own size).
- `SPACING`/`ALIGNMENT`/`CONTENT_MARGINS`/`PADDING` roles.

### 2. `VStack` section — "Layout & sizing" subsection
- **Allocation**: vertical main axis — Fixed exact / Fill expands (leftover only to Fill children) / Hug = sum of children heights + spacing; horizontal cross axis — children hug unless Fill, positioned per `ALIGNMENT`.
- **Spacing**: gap between *adjacent* children only, clamped ≥ 0 (negative → 0).
- **Alignment**: position-only, default Leading (SwiftUI's stack default is Center — noted as a protocol choice).
- **Insets**: `CONTENT_MARGINS` = uniform stack inset; `PADDING` = per-node styling; precedence when both on the same node → per-edge `PADDING_*` > `PADDING` > `CONTENT_MARGINS`. *(Found divergence: render-gtk applies CONTENT_MARGINS *after* PADDING so it wins — status.md gap; HTML applies PADDING last so it wins.)*
- **Own size**: Hug by default (natural); Fixed → exact box; Fill → absorbs parent leftover.
- **Overflow**: content exceeding a Fixed box clips; inside a `ScrollView` it scrolls.
- **Cross-renderer mapping** table: GTK `GtkBox` (spacing + per-child align per `main_axis_align`/`cross_axis_align`), CSS flex column (`gap`, `align-items:flex-start` default), SwiftUI `VStack` (proposed-size model), Compose `Column` (wrap-content cross axis + `fillMaxWidth`).

### 3. `HStack` section
Same, mirrored: horizontal main axis, vertical cross axis (GTK `valign`), CSS `flex-direction:row`.

### 4. Cross-renderer mapping table + edge cases (both)
- SPACING only between children; negative → 0.
- Leftover with no Fill child → empty at the end.
- Alignment positions, never resizes.
- Fill child in a Hug stack collapses to natural.
- Root stacks are typically `Fill` (e.g. `FrameMod.of(FILL, FILL)`); a Hug root hugs its content.

### 5. Status.md sync (AGENTS.md, no code changes)
- `pathland-render-gtk/status.md`: gap — CONTENT_MARGINS currently wins over PADDING (spec: PADDING wins).

## What SwiftUI + Compose agree on (the spec will encode these)

## B. Layout & Container Primitives

Layout primitives arrange children. They carry `SPACING` (0x0001),
`ALIGNMENT` (0x0002), and `CONTENT_MARGINS` (0x0005), plus layout modifiers from
[MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#1-layout). Renderers map them to their native flex
box / grid primitives (GTK `GtkBox`/`GtkGrid`, CSS flex/grid).

### The stack layout model

`VStack`/`HStack` (and the lazy stacks) follow the **SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose
layout model**: a stack *proposes* a size to each child, the child reports its
own size, and the stack *places* it. The protocol transmits **intent** — size
kinds and alignment — never geometry; the renderer resolves the proposal with
its native layout engine. The full allocation contract is
[LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md); the essentials:

**Size kinds.** Each `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` is one of three kinds (LAYOUT.md §size
model):

| Kind | Wire value | Meaning | SwiftUI | Compose |
|------|-----------|---------|---------|---------|
| **Fixed** | finite `F32` | exactly that many points | `.frame(width: 44, height: 44)` | `Modifier.size(44.dp)` |
| **Fill** | `-1` | expand to available space | `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` | `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` |
| **Hug** | `-2` / absent | natural size | ideal size | `wrapContentWidth()` |

**Main vs cross axis.** The **main axis** is the stack's layout direction
(VStack = vertical, HStack = horizontal); the other is the **cross axis**.

**Main-axis allocation.** A child is Fixed (exact box), Fill (expands), or Hug
(natural). **Leftover main-axis space goes only to `Fill` children** (and to
`Spacer`, which is Fill by nature); a stack with no Fill child leaves the
leftover empty at the end. Every other child is packed from the start.

**Cross-axis allocation.** A child keeps its own size on the cross axis and is
**positioned** by `ALIGNMENT` — position-only, it never resizes. The default is
**Leading/Start**; `Fill`(3) means default (hug) positioning, not stretch
(Compose `Column` defaults `Alignment.Start`, `Row` defaults `Alignment.Top`;
SwiftUI's stack default is `.center` — a per-framework difference, all three are
expressible with an explicit `ALIGNMENT`). Only a **`Fill`-sized child**
stretches to the stack's cross size.

**Fill propagation.** A Hug-sized stack that contains a **`Fill`-sized child or
`Spacer` on an axis is itself `Fill`-sized on that axis** — the child's
expansion propagates to the stack, which then fills its parent's proposal on
that axis. This matches both reference frameworks:

- SwiftUI `VStack { Button().frame(maxWidth: .infinity) }` fills the width.
- Compose `Column { Box(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) }` fills the width.
- `VStack { Spacer() }` fills the proposed height.

A full-width row is therefore expressed as a `Fill`-width child (or `Spacer`)
inside the stack, never by stretching the stack itself.

**Spacing.** `SPACING` is a fixed gap between **adjacent** children (never
before the first or after the last), clamped to ≥ 0. It matches SwiftUI
`VStack(spacing:)` and Compose `Arrangement.spacedBy(...)`. Leftover space is
distributed by `Fill` children / `Spacer`, never by the gap.

**Insets.** `CONTENT_MARGINS` is the stack's uniform content inset
(equivalently, `PADDING` on the stack). Both compose; when both are present on
the same node, precedence is per-edge `PADDING_*` > `PADDING` >
`CONTENT_MARGINS`.

**Overflow.** A stack with a Fixed box clips content that exceeds it; a stack
inside a `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls.

### VStack — `VSTACK` 0x10

Vertical flex stack. **Properties**: `SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT` (enum: `Leading`=0,
`Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3), `CONTENT_MARGINS`.

**Layout & sizing**

- **Main axis (vertical)**: children are allocated per the stack model —
  Fixed exact, Fill expands (leftover only to `Fill`/`Spacer`), Hug natural. A
  Hug VStack's height is the sum of its children's heights plus `SPACING`
  between them.
- **Cross axis (horizontal)**: children keep their own width (a Fixed box, or a
  Hug natural width); `Fill`-width children stretch to the stack's width. Narrow
  children are positioned per `ALIGNMENT` (default Leading/Start).
- **Own size**: Hug by default (height = content + spacing; width = widest
  child). A Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` makes the box exact; a `Fill` axis — or fill
  propagation — expands to the parent's proposal. A `Fill`-width child makes
  the stack full-width; a `Fill`-height child makes it full-height.
- **Renderer mapping**:

  | Pathland | GTK4 | CSS | SwiftUI | Compose |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `SPACING` | `GtkBox` spacing | `gap` | `VStack(spacing:)` | `Arrangement.spacedBy` |
  | `ALIGNMENT` | per-child cross-axis `halign` (default Start) | `align-items` (default `flex-start`) | `VStack(alignment:)` (default `.center`) | `Column(horizontalAlignment)` (default `Start`) |
  | Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` | `set_size_request` + hug | `width`/`height` px | `.frame(width:height:)` | `Modifier.size` |
  | `FILL` | `hexpand`/`vexpand` + Fill | `100%` / `flex-grow` | `.frame(maxWidth/maxHeight: .infinity)` | `fillMaxWidth/Height` |
  | `SPACER` | expanding empty box | `flex: 1` | `Spacer()` | `Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))` |

- **Edge cases**: negative `SPACING` → 0; no Fill child + leftover → empty at
  the end; a Fixed-width child narrower than the stack keeps its exact box and
  is aligned; a `Fill` child in a Hug stack propagates (fills the parent's
  proposal); root stacks are typically `Fill` (`FrameMod.of(FILL, FILL)`).

### HStack — `HSTACK` 0x11

Horizontal flex stack. Same properties as `VStack`, mirrored:

- **Main axis (horizontal)**: children per the stack model — Fixed exact, Fill
  expands (leftover only to `Fill`/`Spacer`), Hug natural. A Hug HStack's width
  is the sum of its children's widths plus `SPACING`.
- **Cross axis (vertical)**: children keep their own height (Fixed or Hug);
  `Fill`-height children stretch. Positioned per `ALIGNMENT` (default
  Leading/Start → GTK `valign`, CSS `align-items:flex-start`, Compose `Row`
  default `Alignment.Top`; SwiftUI `.center`).
- **Own size**: Hug by default (width = content + spacing; height = tallest
  child); a Fixed box exact; `Fill`/propagation expands.
- **Renderer mapping**: as VStack, with GTK `GtkBox` horizontal + per-child
  `valign`, CSS `flex-direction:row`, SwiftUI `HStack(alignment:spacing:)`,
  Compose `Row` (`Arrangement.spacedBy`, `verticalAlignment`).
- **Edge cases**: as VStack.

### ZStack — `ZSTACK` 0x12

Depth-overlapping layer stack: children are drawn in depth order — **child index =
draw order**, later = on top. **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (enum: `Leading`=0,
`Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3), plus layout modifiers (Fixed/Fill
`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, `PADDING`, `CONTENT_MARGINS` as an inset). **No `SPACING`** —
children occupy the same box by design; there is no gap between them.

**Layout & sizing** (SwiftUI `ZStack` / Compose `Box` semantics)

- **Overlay allocation**: unlike a flex stack, children do **not** add to each
  other along an axis — they share one box. Each child keeps its own size (a
  Fixed box, or a Hug natural size) and is **positioned** by `ALIGNMENT` on
  **both axes**; only a **`Fill`-sized child** stretches to the stack's size.
- **Own size**: the stack **hugs to its largest child** by default — on each
  axis its size is the **maximum** of its children's sizes, never the sum. A
  Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` makes the box exact; a `Fill` axis — or fill
  propagation (a `Fill` child on an axis makes the Hug stack `Fill` on that
  axis, see the stack layout model above) — expands to the parent's proposal.
  `ZStack { Color.red }` fills (Color is layout-greedy); `ZStack { Text("hi") }`
  hugs the text.
- **Alignment**: `ALIGNMENT` positions each child on **both** axes. The
  single-axis enum is applied to both axes: `Leading`(0) = top-leading
  (Start × Start), `Center`(1) = centered, `Trailing`(2) = bottom-trailing
  (End × End), `Fill`(3) / absent = default hug positioning (Leading).
  Position-only: it never resizes a child. SwiftUI's `ZStack(alignment:)`
  defaults to `.center`; Compose `Box(contentAlignment:)` defaults to
  `Alignment.TopStart`; the protocol default is **Leading** (Start × Start,
  Compose parity). A mixed-axis alignment (e.g. top-trailing) is a future
  extension — today `ALIGNMENT` is a single code applied to both axes.
- **Overflow**: content that exceeds a Fixed box is clipped to the stack.

  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | ZStack | `GtkOverlay` | `position:relative` container + `position:absolute` children | `ZStack(alignment:)` | `Box(contentAlignment:)` |

  the same size model (a Fixed first child keeps its exact box; a `Fill` one
  stretches); draw order is always child index; a `Fill` child in a Hug ZStack

387: layout model**: a stack *proposes* a size to each child, the child reports its

content.text:
Audit complete. Here's the gap report — spec (`PRIMITIVES.md` VStack/HStack/ZStack) vs the two renderers (+ the TS DOM client).

## Gap audit

### High severity

**G1 — Fill propagation: not implemented (render-gtk + render-html/TS).**
Spec: a Hug stack with a `Fill` child/`Spacer` on an axis becomes `Fill` on that axis and fills its parent's proposal.
- GTK: a `hexpand/vexpand` child in a Hug `GtkBox` claims nothing → box hugs, child collapses to natural.
- HTML/TS: `width:100%`/`height:100%` on a child of a content-sized flex container resolves to the content size; `flex-grow` exists only on Spacer.
Breaks the core SwiftUI/Compose full-width-row pattern. *(already in both status.md)*

**G2 — GTK "Fixed" is a *minimum*, not an exact box; Fixed-width Text doesn't wrap.**
Spec: Fixed = exact points box; content fits inside.
- `set_size_request(w,h)` is a minimum; a child whose natural size exceeds it (long Text, a stack wider than its box) is allocated natural → box ≠ requested.
- `apply_text_style` (lib.rs:1840) sets only font-size/color — **no wrap, no max-width-chars** from `WIDTH`. A Fixed-width Text renders at its full natural width.

**G3 — ZStack model: unimplemented in both renderers.**
- GTK (`sync_overlay_children`): first child pinned via `set_child` → GtkOverlay **expands it to fill regardless of size kind**; overlay `ALIGNMENT` not applied (children sit natural-size top-left); overlay hugs rather than honoring a Fixed box.
- HTML/TS: container emitted `width:100%;height:100%` (greedy both axes, not Hug-to-largest-child); children wrapped `position:absolute;inset:0` with **no `ALIGNMENT` positioning**.

**G4 — GTK text constraints unimplemented: `LINE_LIMIT` / `TRUNCATION_MODE`.**
No `ellipsize`/wrap/clamp anywhere in render-gtk (HTML/TS do it via `-webkit-line-clamp` + nowrap+ellipsis). Adjacent to layout (a line-limited text's box size differs).

### Medium severity

**G5 — Cross-axis `Fill` in HTML/TS relies on `100%`, which fails when the container's cross size is content-driven.** Spec: only `Fill` children stretch to the container's cross size. `height:100%` of an *indefinite* height is ignored; `align-self:stretch` would be correct but needs per-container orientation awareness (not currently threaded through `render_node`).

**G6 — Fixed-box overflow clipping: neither renderer clips.** Spec: "a Fixed box clips content that exceeds it." GTK has no `set_overflow` anywhere; HTML/TS clip only via `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`. **Open decision** — SwiftUI doesn't clip a fixed frame unless `.clipped()`, so this may be a *spec* refinement (clip only with `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`) rather than a renderer gap.

### Low severity

**G7 — GTK Spacer expands both axes** (`hexpand`+`vexpand` on the Spacer box, lib.rs:1333); spec says Spacer is greedy main-axis only. HTML Spacer (`flex:1`) is correct.

**G8 — CONTENT_MARGINS wins over PADDING in GTK.** `apply_padding` runs before `apply_style` (which applies CONTENT_MARGINS) → CONTENT_MARGINS overrides; spec requires `PADDING > CONTENT_MARGINS`. HTML/TS conform. *(already in render-gtk status.md)*

## Proposed remediation plan

| Phase | Work | Renderers |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Fill propagation: a Hug stack with a Fill/Spacer child fills that axis | render-gtk (`layout.rs` + stack sizing), render-html (`render_node` orientation-aware), TS DOM client |
| **2** | ZStack: first-child size model, per-child `ALIGNMENT` (both axes), Hug-to-largest-child own size | render-gtk (`sync_overlay_children`), render-html/TS (container sizing + child positioning) |
| **3** | GTK text: wrap at Fixed width, `LINE_LIMIT`/`TRUNCATION_MODE` | render-gtk (`apply_text_style`) |
| **4** | Cross-axis `Fill` via `align-self:stretch` (orientation-aware) | render-html + TS |
| **5** | Spacer main-axis-only in GTK; CONTENT_MARGINS precedence | render-gtk |

Plus one decision (G6): refine the spec (Fixed box clips only with `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`) or make renderers clip.

Which phases should I plan in detail to execute first — and how do you want G6 resolved?
g6: Align with swiftui

G6 resolved: **align with SwiftUI** — a Fixed box *constrains layout but does not clip*; overflow is drawn outside the box unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` is set (SwiftUI `.clipped()` parity). That makes it a **spec refinement** (not a renderer change), plus it exposes one real renderer gap (GTK never implements `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`).

Here's the consolidated plan.

## Part A — G6 spec refinement (SwiftUI parity)

- `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` **stack model "Overflow"** bullet: "a stack with a Fixed box clips content that exceeds it" → *"a Fixed box constrains layout; content that exceeds it is drawn outside the box unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it (SwiftUI `.clipped()` parity)."*
- `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` **ZStack "Overflow"** bullet: same wording.
- `spec/LAYOUT.md` "A container that is itself Fixed" overflow line: align ("scrolls for a ScrollView, otherwise overflow is visible unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`").
- `render-gtk/status.md`: add gap — `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` unimplemented (no `set_overflow`/clip anywhere).

## Part B — renderer gap fixes (phased)

**Phase 1 — Fill propagation** (G1, both renderers + TS): a Hug stack with a Fill/Spacer child on an axis becomes Fill on that axis.
- render-gtk: in `layout.rs`, decide the stack's own axis size from its children (a Fill child ⇒ stack fills on that axis); thread it into the parent's `main_axis_align`/`cross_axis_align` via the child-node lookup already there.
- render-html/TS: orientation-aware `render_node` — a Fill child on the cross axis gets `align-self:stretch`; on the main axis keep `flex:1`-style grow; a Hug stack with a Fill child emits greedy (this partially resolves G5 too).

**Phase 2 — ZStack** (G3, both): first-child honors the size model (GTK: stop forcing the main child to fill; set per-overlay `halign`/`valign` from `ALIGNMENT`); HTML/TS: container hugs to the largest child, children keep their size and are positioned per `ALIGNMENT` (drop the blanket `inset:0` fill).

**Phase 3 — GTK text** (G2/G4): wrap a `Label` at a Fixed width (`set_wrap` + width), and implement `LINE_LIMIT` (`set_lines`/`ellipsize`) + `TRUNCATION_MODE` (`ellipsize`).

**Phase 4 — cross-axis Fill** (G5): the orientation-aware `align-self:stretch` from Phase 1 in render-html/TS.

**Phase 5 — GTK cleanups** (G7/G8 + `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`): Spacer greedy main-axis only; `PADDING` over `CONTENT_MARGINS`; `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` → `set_overflow(Hidden)`.

Each phase: extend the pure decision tests (`layout.rs`) / HTML conformance assertions, update the affected `status.md`.

## Open question
Which scope for this pass — **Phase 1 + 2** (the two core layout-model gaps, recommended) in one pass, or the full Phase 1–5 sweep? And confirm the Part A spec-refinement edits go in alongside.

Phase 2 render-html SSR: ZStack grid-based hug + per-child ALIGNMENT

Committed as `d28752da` on `spec/core-components-layout`.

## What landed

**Part A — G6 (SwiftUI parity):** Fixed boxes now *constrain but don't clip* — overflow draws outside unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` (`PRIMITIVES.md` + `LAYOUT.md`); `render-gtk` `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` gap noted.

**Phase 1 — fill propagation (both renderers + DOM client):**
- `render-gtk`: `layout::effective_fill` — a Hug stack/ZStack with a `FILL` child / `Spacer` / greedy primitive on an axis becomes `FILL` on that axis (so `VStack { Spacer() }` fills height, `Column { fillMaxWidth() }` fills width).
- `render-html` SSR + TS DOM client: `fills_axis` emits `width/height:100%` on propagated axes; cross-axis `FILL` children stretch via `align-self:stretch`; the DOM mirrors with a derived-layout pass after every batch.

**Phase 2 — ZStack (both):**
- GTK: every child is an overlay keeping its own size unless effectively `FILL`, positioned by `ALIGNMENT` on both axes (the first-child-pinned-to-fill `GtkOverlay` main-child is gone); hugs to its largest child.
- HTML/TS: an overlapping grid (`grid-area:1/1`); container hugs (`max-content`) unless Fixed/FILL/propagated; children positioned per `ALIGNMENT`.

**Verification:** Rust workspace (30 suites, incl. new `fill_propagates_through_a_hug_stack`), TS (175, incl. conformance + shell-drift guards), golden SSR fixtures regenerated, `dom-renderer.js` rebuilt into both demos. Status.md files updated.

Remaining gaps still tracked: GTK `CONTENT_MARGINS`/`PADDING` precedence, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, GTK Fixed-box-is-minimum/text-wrap (Phases 3–5).

- **At creation**: `stack_widget` (lib.rs:1631) → `GtkBox::new(orientation, layout.spacing)`.
- **On every frame**: `update`'s `WidgetKind::Stack` case (lib.rs:338-343) re-applies `bx.set_spacing(l.spacing)` (VSTACK/HSTACK/LAZY all map to `WidgetKind::Stack`, lib.rs:1062-1065).
- GTK4 `GtkBox` spacing = a gap between **adjacent** children, clamped ≥ 0 in `stack_layout` — exactly the spec's "gap between adjacent children." The Java DSL emits `SPACING` (VStack.java:61-63), so the value reaches the box.

So a `VStack(spacing: 14)` renders a 14pt gap in GTK.

## But render-gtk genuinely doesn't respect spacing in two places

1. **`GRID` / `LAZY_VGRID` / `LAZY_HGRID`** — real bug. `SPACING` is documented for grids (PRIMITIVES.md), but `sync_grid_children` (lib.rs:769) never sets `row_spacing`/`column_spacing` on the `GtkGrid`. 2. **Composite control body boxes** — `sync_composite_children` (lib.rs:269) hardcodes the body `GtkBox` spacing to `0`. It's usually moot (the DSL wraps a control's children in an HStack/VStack that carries its own spacing), but a control with *multiple direct children and no wrapping stack* loses the gap.

I've traced the code path thoroughly. Here's my analysis and a plan.

## Analysis: why GTK spreads the rows

The layout contract is enforced in `sync_stack_children` (lib.rs:735): for each child of the rows VStack (vertical), it sets `set_valign(main)` where `main = main_axis_align(button, Vertical, tree)` = **`Align::Start`** (the button has WIDTH=FILL only — `FrameMod.of(width)` is width-only — so its vertical size kind is Hug; it's not greedy and not a propagating container). The trailing `Spacer` (greedy main-axis) is the only child that should absorb leftover. So statically, the rows *should* hug to the top.

The **only way** a `GtkBox` spreads leftover between the row buttons is if they are effectively `valign=Fill`/`vexpand` at render time. The suspect: `apply_style` (lib.rs:1794) sets `set_hexpand(true)` + `set_halign(Fill)` for the FILL-width buttons but **leaves `valign`/`vexpand` at GTK's default `Fill`** for the absent-height axis; `sync_stack_children` then sets `valign=Start`, but **never resets `vexpand`**, and GTK4's box can treat a `Fill`-aligned child as expandable. If the per-child `valign=Start` isn't winning (a reconcile-order subtlety, or GTK expansion semantics), the buttons share the leftover → rows "spread out." HTML is correct because it never stretches them.

## Plan: make GTK expansion match the effective-Fill decision exactly

**1. Fix `sync_stack_children` (render-gtk, lib.rs:735-766):** in the per-child loop, in addition to `set_halign`/`set_valign`, explicitly set the expand flags from the same decision:
- `w.set_vexpand(main == Align::Fill)` (main axis — vertical here)
- `w.set_hexpand(cross == Align::Fill)` (cross axis)

This makes a non-FILL main-axis child (`vexpand=false`, `valign=Start`) *unable* to claim leftover — it is the exact SwiftUI/Compose contract ("leftover goes only to FILL children / Spacer") and is immune to any residual GTK-default expansion. The trailing `Spacer` keeps `vexpand=true` (its main-axis decision is Fill), so it still absorbs the leftover and pins the rows to the top. `apply_style`'s `set_hexpand(true)` for FILL-width is still correct (cross = Fill → hexpand true, consistent).

**2. Update the pure tests** (`layout.rs`): the `main_axis_align`/`cross_axis_align` decisions are already covered; add an assertion documenting that a Hug-height child in a vertical stack is non-expanding (Start, never stretched) — the FILL-propagates test already covers the positive case.

**3. Status + verification:** update `render-gtk/status.md` (main-axis expansion now explicitly synced per child; rows pin to top via the Spacer). 123: ### Rationale
124: 
125: These rules are the bugs-fixed-and-avoided model of the GTK renderer:
126: 
127: - A **Fixed image** in a row stays its box (never scaled to content or stretched
128:   by a tall row).
129: - A **Fixed/Hug child in a `Fill` container** keeps its size; leftover space
130:   goes to `Fill` children (or stays empty).
131: - A **composite button** (e.g. a library row) sizes to its content on the main
132:   axis unless the node is explicitly `Fill`.

136: ## Content fitting
137: 
138: Content-bearing views fit their content **inside** their allocated box:
139: 
140: - **Media** (`IMAGE`, `VIDEO`, and the visual of `AUDIO`): fitted per
141:   `CONTENT_MODE` — `Fit` (0) scales to contain (letterboxed), `Fill` (1) scales
142:   to cover (cropped). The box is the allocation, never the content's intrinsic
143:   size.
144: - **Text**: wraps within a Fixed width; `LINE_LIMIT` / `TRUNCATION_MODE` apply
145:   within the box. A Hug text takes its natural (wrapped) size.
146: - **Containers** (stacks, scroll): children lay out inside; a Fixed box
147:   constrains them (scroll for `SCROLLVIEW`, clip otherwise).

Confirmed — you're right. For both #2 and #3 I derived the contract from the HTML renderer / TS client, because the spec leaves too much open. Here's the audit and a plan to make the spec self-sufficient.

## What the spec currently pins vs. what's missing

| Behavior | Spec says | Missing (had to infer from HTML/TS) |
|---|---|---|
| **`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`** | MODIFIERS.md:211+224 ("`SHAPE_KIND` selects the clip geometry; `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`(1) turns clipping on"); LAYOUT.md:120 "drawn outside unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it" | What "clip" means: a **post-layout visual clip to the allocated bounds box** (both axes, content + own painting), layout unaffected, default off, `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls instead. |
| **Text wrapping** | LAYOUT.md:144 "wraps within a Fixed width… A Hug text takes its natural (wrapped) size" | When wrapping happens (only when width is constrained; a Hug text is a **single line**, not "wrapped"); word-boundary breaking; natural height = lines × line height. |
| **`LINE_LIMIT`** | MODIFIERS.md:185 "0 means unlimited" | Positive N caps lines **with a tail ellipsis** on the last visible line; wraps up to N lines when width-constrained. |
| **`TRUNCATION_MODE`** | MODIFIERS.md:162+418 (codes only) | Positions the ellipsis (Head/Middle/Tail); interaction with `LINE_LIMIT`/width; and one semantic decision (below). |

## Plan: pin the "content fitting, truncation & clipping" contract in the spec

Expand **LAYOUT.md §Content fitting** into a precise contract (the single authoritative home), then tighten the MODIFIERS.md semantics notes and the PRIMITIVES.md Text/Image sections to reference it. Proposed contract:

- **Text wrapping** — unconstrained Text = single line at natural width; wraps at **word boundaries** only when its width is constrained (Fixed `WIDTH`, or `LINE_LIMIT` needing multiple lines); unbreakable words break by character; natural height = line count × line height; Fixed `HEIGHT` constrains and overflow follows the G6 rule (visible unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`).
- **`LINE_LIMIT`** — positive N clamps to **at most N lines**, any overflow replaced by `…` at the end of the last visible line; 0/absent = unlimited; does not force single-line.
- **`TRUNCATION_MODE`** — `Head`=0 / `Middle`=1 / `Tail`=2 sets the ellipsis position **whenever truncation occurs** (a `LINE_LIMIT` clamp, or a width-constrained single-line truncation).
- **`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`** — a post-layout visual clip to the node's allocated bounds box (both axes, content + own decoration); layout unaffected; default off; `SHAPE_KIND` constrains the clip geometry; a `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls instead.
- Add **conformance cases** to LAYOUT.md (C7: Fixed-width Text wraps; C8: `LINE_LIMIT` clamps with ellipsis; C9: `TRUNCATION_MODE` position; C10: `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips to the box) as the cross-renderer targets.

## One decision needed

**Does `TRUNCATION_MODE` alone (no `LINE_LIMIT`, no Fixed width) force a single line?**
- **(a) SwiftUI-aligned** — it only positions the ellipsis when truncation is already happening; alone it has no effect. *Requires* changing HTML/TS (currently `nowrap`+ellipsis for trunc-alone) and the GTK code I just wrote.
- **(b) Keep the current renderer contract** — `TRUNCATION_MODE` alone implies single-line truncation (HTML does `nowrap`, GTK now does `set_wrap(false)`). Slight divergence from SwiftUI, but no renderer change.

Which do you prefer — and is this pass **spec-only** (pin the contract + status notes), or **spec + renderer alignment** (reconcile renderers to the pinned contract)?
a. spec only first
Decision locked: **SwiftUI-aligned `TRUNCATION_MODE`**, spec-only pass. Let me verify the exact anchor points in the spec before finalizing the plan.

## Plan: pin the content-fitting / truncation / clipping contract (spec-only, SwiftUI-aligned)

### 1. `spec/LAYOUT.md` — expand §Content fitting (L136–147) into the authoritative contract
- **Text wrapping**: unconstrained Text = **single line at its natural width**; it **wraps at word boundaries only when its width is constrained** (a Fixed `WIDTH`, or a `LINE_LIMIT` needing multiple lines); unbreakable words break by character; natural height = line count × line height; a Fixed `HEIGHT` constrains it and overflow follows the overflow rule.
- **`LINE_LIMIT`**: positive N clamps to **at most N lines**, overflow replaced by `…` at the end of the last visible line (tail ellipsis); 0/absent = unlimited; does not force single-line (lines form by wrapping at the available width + explicit breaks).
- **`TRUNCATION_MODE`** (Head=0/Middle=1/Tail=2): **positions that ellipsis** (start / middle / end of the last visible line). It applies **only when a `LINE_LIMIT` clamp truncates** — alone it has **no observable effect** (SwiftUI-aligned); it never forces single-line or truncates by itself.
- **`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`**: a **post-layout visual clip** — the node's content *and* its own painted decoration clip to its **allocated bounds box** (both axes); layout is unaffected (still allocated/positioned as unclipped); default off; a `SHAPE_KIND` carried alongside constrains the clip geometry (bare `.clipped()` = bounds box); a `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls instead.

### 2. `spec/LAYOUT.md` — conformance cases
- Fix **C6** (stale after G6): "children lay out within `200`; overflow is **visible unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`**".
- Add **C7** Fixed-width `Text` wraps within the box · **C8** `LINE_LIMIT=2` → at most 2 lines, last line tail-ellipsized · **C9** `LINE_LIMIT=1` + `TRUNCATION_MODE=Head` → single line, ellipsis at the start · **C10** `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS=1` clips overflow to the box.

### 3. `spec/MODIFIERS.md` — semantics notes (L185, L224–227)
Replace the thin `LINE_LIMIT` note; add a `TRUNCATION_MODE` note (positions the ellipsis; effective only under a `LINE_LIMIT` clamp); expand the `.clipped()`/`clipShape` note to define the post-layout visual clip. Each references LAYOUT.md.

### 4. `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` — Text section (L232–244)

## Content fitting, truncation & clipping

Content-bearing views fit their content **inside** their allocated box:

- **Media** (`IMAGE`, `VIDEO`, and the visual of `AUDIO`): fitted per
  `CONTENT_MODE` — `Fit` (0) scales to contain (letterboxed), `Fill` (1) scales
  to cover (cropped). The box is the allocation, never the content's intrinsic
  size.

### Text

- **Wrapping.** An unconstrained `TEXT` lays out on a **single line at its
  natural width**. It **wraps at word boundaries only when its width is
  constrained** — a Fixed `WIDTH`, or a `LINE_LIMIT` that needs multiple lines.
  An unbreakable word wider than the box may break by character. A wrapped
  Text's natural height is its **line count × line height** (so a Hug container
  can compute its size). A Fixed `HEIGHT` constrains the box; overflow follows
  the overflow rules ([above](#a-container-that-is-itself-fixed)).
- **`LINE_LIMIT`.** A positive `LINE_LIMIT` (N) clamps the rendered text to **at
  most N lines**; any overflow beyond the last visible line is replaced by an
  ellipsis `…` at its end (**tail** truncation). `0`/absent = unlimited. It does
  not force a single line — lines are formed by wrapping at the available width
  and by explicit line breaks.
- **`TRUNCATION_MODE`.** `Head`=0, `Middle`=1, `Tail`=2 **positions the
  ellipsis** (at the start / middle / end of the last visible line) whenever a
  `LINE_LIMIT` clamp truncates. It applies **only when such a clamp truncates**:
  on its own it has **no observable effect** (SwiftUI-aligned) — it never forces
  a single line and never truncates by itself.

### Clipping — `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`

`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` (0x1010, U8) is a **post-layout visual clip**: the node's
content and its own painted decoration (fills, backgrounds, borders) are
clipped to its **allocated bounds box** — on **both axes**. Layout is
unaffected: the node is still allocated and positioned exactly as if unclipped;
only what is painted is clipped. `0`/absent = no clipping. A `SHAPE_KIND`
(0x0006) carried alongside constrains the clip to that geometry instead of the
plain bounds box (a bare `.clipped()` is `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` with no shape, so the
clip is the bounds box). A `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls its content rather than
clipping it.

### Containers

Stacks, scroll, and other containers lay their children out inside; a Fixed box
constrains them (scroll for `SCROLLVIEW`, otherwise overflow is visible unless
`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it).

## The contract is now pinned in the spec (spec-only, SwiftUI-aligned)

**`spec/LAYOUT.md`** — §Content fitting is now "Content fitting, truncation & clipping", the authoritative contract:
- **Text wrapping**: unconstrained = single line at natural width; wraps at word boundaries only when width-constrained (Fixed `WIDTH` or `LINE_LIMIT`); natural height = lines × line height.
- **`LINE_LIMIT`**: positive N clamps to at most N lines with a **tail ellipsis**; 0/absent = unlimited; doesn't force single-line.

- **`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`**: a **post-layout visual clip** of content + painted decoration to the allocated bounds box (both axes); layout unaffected; `SHAPE_KIND` constrains geometry; `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls instead.

**Conformance**: C6 corrected (overflow visible unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`), new **C7–C10** (wrap / line-limit ellipsis / truncation position / clipping).

**Cross-references**: MODIFIERS.md `LINE_LIMIT`/`TRUNCATION_MODE`/`clipShape` semantics now point to the contract; PRIMITIVES.md Text section gained a "Content fitting" line.

**Renderer divergence flagged** (both `status.md`): `TRUNCATION_MODE` alone currently forces a single line (`nowrap`+ellipsis in HTML; `set_wrap(false)`+ellipsize in GTK) — a later alignment pass will reconcile them to the pinned contract.

## Next step: align the renderers to the pinned content-fitting contract (Option A — recommended)

We just pinned the contract spec-first; `status.md` in both renderers flags the alignment as pending. This closes the loop: **`TRUNCATION_MODE` alone must stop forcing a single line** (the one divergence), and the rest of the contract (wrap / `LINE_LIMIT` / `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`) gets verified as conformant.

### The divergence to fix (both renderers)
| Renderer | Current (wrong) | Pinned contract |
|---|---|---|
| `render-gtk` `apply_text_style` (lib.rs:1928) | `trunc.is_some() → set_wrap(false)` + ellipsize | TRUNCATION alone has **no effect**; ellipsize only under a `LINE_LIMIT` clamp |
| `render-html` SSR (element_css:388) | TRUNCATION present → `nowrap`+ellipsis | same — no standalone effect |
| TS DOM client (classes.ts:292) | `textOverflow` on TRUNCATION | same — gate on the clamp |

### Plan
1. **render-gtk**: remove the `trunc → set_wrap(false)` branch; wrap when `fixed_width || line_limit>0`; ellipsize only when truncating (`line_limit>0` → `set_lines(n)` + `ellipsize(trunc mode or Tail)`). Update the `ellipsize_from` usage + tests.
2. **render-html SSR + TS**: drop the `TRUNCATION_MODE → nowrap+ellipsis` block / `textOverflow` handler; keep `LINE_LIMIT>0 → line-clamp` (tail ellipsis). Regenerate SSR fixtures; update any test asserting the old behavior (SSR/DOM stay canonical).
3. **Conformance**: add cheap renderer checks for **C7** (Fixed-width Text wraps), **C8** (line-limit tail ellipsis), **C9** (single-line Head), **C10** (`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips, layout unchanged) — HTML assertions + GTK pure checks where possible.

### One decision needed first — Head/Middle fidelity on multi-line clamps
`TRUNCATION_MODE=Head/Middle` on a **multi-line** clamp (a `LINE_LIMIT>1` wrap): native support is limited — CSS `line-clamp` only tail-ellipsizes; GTK `set_lines`+`EllipsizeMode::Start/Middle` only works reliably for **single-line** labels. So strict Head/Middle on multi-line isn't achievable everywhere. Options:
- **(a) Best-effort, renderer-owned**: Tail works everywhere; Head/Middle implemented where the native text system supports it (GTK single-line `Start`/`Middle`); otherwise falls back to Tail, documented per renderer. Spec stays as-is (the semantic target).
- **(b) Amend the spec**: `TRUNCATION_MODE`'s `Head`/`Middle` apply to **single-line truncation** (`LINE_LIMIT=1` or a single-line box); multi-line clamps always tail-ellipsize. Fully implementable everywhere; a small edit to the just-pinned LAYOUT.md/MODIFIERS.md text.

## Plan: Option A — align renderers to the pinned content-fitting contract (renderer-owned Head/Middle)

No spec changes (decision a keeps the spec as the semantic target).

### 1. `render-gtk` — `apply_text_style` (lib.rs:1914–1938)
- **Remove** `else if trunc.is_some() { label.set_wrap(false); }` → `TRUNCATION_MODE` alone no longer forces a single line.
- **Wrap** when `fixed_width || line_limit.is_some_and(|n| n > 0)`.
- **Ellipsize only under a `LINE_LIMIT` clamp** (a clamp is the only thing that truncates): `set_lines(n)` + `set_ellipsize(trunc.map(ellipsize_from).unwrap_or(End))`.
- `TRUNCATION_MODE` alone → no wrap change, no ellipsize (no observable effect).
- Renderer-owned fidelity already in place: `ellipsize_from` maps Head/Middle/Tail → `Start/Middle/End` (reliable single-line, best-effort multi-line). Update the test/comment.

### 2. `render-html` SSR — `element_css` (lib.rs:388–391)
- **Delete** the `TRUNCATION_MODE present → text-overflow:ellipsis;overflow:hidden;white-space:nowrap` block.
- Keep `LINE_LIMIT>0 → line-clamp` (render_node:1024) — that's the tail ellipsis (C8). CSS can't position a head/middle ellipsis, so non-Tail modes fall back to Tail (documented in status.md).

### 3. TS DOM client — `classes.ts`
- `PROP_TRUNCATION_MODE` → no-op (consume but ignore); remove the now-unused `truncationCss` (L155–160, no tests reference it).
